   103→class Diagnostician:
   104→    """LLM-based failure diagnosis."""
   105→
   106→    def __init__(self):
   107→        self._known_issues: dict[str, DiagnosisResult] = {
   108→            "high_latency": DiagnosisResult(
   109→                component="swarm",
   110→                issue="High response latency",
   111→                probable_cause="Model overloaded or insufficient resources",
   112→                recommended_action="Switch to smaller model or increase timeout",
   113→                confidence=0.8,
   114→            ),
   115→            "low_quality": DiagnosisResult(
   116→                component="swarm",
   117→                issue="Low response quality",
   118→                probable_cause="Model not suited for task type",
   119→                recommended_action="Benchmark alternatives and swap model",
   120→                confidence=0.7,
   121→            ),
   122→            "connection_failed": DiagnosisResult(
   123→                component="ollama",
   124→                issue="Connection to Ollama failed",
   125→                probable_cause="Ollama service not running",
   126→                recommended_action="Restart Ollama: ollama serve",
   127→                confidence=0.9,
   128→            ),
   129→            "sandbox_divergence": DiagnosisResult(
   130→                component="sandbox",
   131→                issue="Sandbox simulation divergence detected",
   132→                probable_cause="Numerical instability or HIHO coherence drift in simulation",
   133→                recommended_action="Restart sandbox with tighter divergence thresholds",
   134→                confidence=0.85,
   135→            ),
   136→        }
   137→
   138→    def diagnose(self, health_status: HealthStatus) -> DiagnosisResult:
   139→        """Diagnose a health issue."""
   140→        # Pattern matching on known issues
   141→        if health_status.metric == "latency_ms" and health_status.status == "failing":
   142→            return self._known_issues["high_latency"]
   143→
   144→        if health_status.metric == "quality_score" and health_status.status in (
   145→            "degraded",
   146→            "failing",
   147→        ):
   148→            return self._known_issues["low_quality"]
   149→
   150→        if health_status.component == "ollama" and health_status.status == "failing":
   151→            return self._known_issues["connection_failed"]
   152→
   153→        if health_status.component == "sandbox" and health_status.metric == "divergence":
   154→            return self._known_issues["sandbox_divergence"]
   155→
   156→        # Generic diagnosis
   157→        return DiagnosisResult(
   158→            component=health_status.component,
   159→            issue=f"{health_status.metric} {health_status.status}",
   160→            probable_cause="Unknown - requires investigation",
   161→            recommended_action="Check logs and component health",
   162→            confidence=0.3,
   163→        )
   164→
   165→
   166→class Corrector:
   167→    """Autonomous correction of detected issues."""
   168→
   169→    def __init__(self):
   170→        self._corrections: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   171→
   172→    async def apply_correction(self, diagnosis: DiagnosisResult) -> bool:
   173→        """Apply automatic correction based on diagnosis."""
   174→        correction = {
   175→            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
   176→            "component": diagnosis.component,
   177→            "issue": diagnosis.issue,
   178→            "action": diagnosis.recommended_action,
   179→            "applied": False,
   180→        }
   181→
   182→        # Auto-corrections we can apply
   183→        if "swap model" in diagnosis.recommended_action.lower():
   184→            # Trigger model manager to benchmark and swap
   185→            from cohezion.swarm.model_manager import get_manager
   186→
   187→            get_manager()
   188→            # Mark as needing swap - actual swap happens on next call
   189→            correction["applied"] = True
   190→            logger.info(f"Scheduled model swap for {diagnosis.component}")
   191→
   192→        self._corrections.append(correction)
   193→        self._save_log()
   194→
   195→        return correction["applied"]
   196→
   197→    def _save_log(self) -> None:
   198→        """Save correction history."""
   199→        HEALTH_LOG_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   200→        HEALTH_LOG_PATH.write_text(
   201→            json.dumps(
   202→                {
   203→                    "corrections": self._corrections[-100:],
   204→                },
   205→                indent=2,
   206→            )
   207→        )
   208→
   209→    def get_history(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   210→        """Get correction history."""
   211→        return self._corrections
   212→
   213→
   214→class SelfHealingSystem:
   215→    """
   216→    Complete self-healing system.
   217→
   218→    Integrates:
   219→    - Drift detection
   220→    - LLM-based diagnosis
   221→    - Autonomous correction
   222→    """
   223→
   224→    def __init__(self):
   225→        self.detector = DriftDetector()
   226→        self.diagnostician = Diagnostician()
   227→        self.corrector = Corrector()
   228→
   229→    async def health_check(self) -> list[HealthStatus]:
   230→        """Run full system health check."""
   231→        issues = []
   232→
   233→        # Check Ollama
   234→        try:
   235→            import httpx
   236→
   237→            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
   238→                resp = await client.get("http://localhost:11434/api/tags")
   239→                ollama_healthy = resp.status_code == 200
   240→        except Exception:
   241→            ollama_healthy = False
   242→
   243→        status = self.detector.check("ollama", "available", 1.0 if ollama_healthy else 0.0, 0.1)
   244→        if status.status != "healthy":
   245→            issues.append(status)
   246→
   247→        # Check SurrealDB
   248→        try:
   249→            import httpx
   250→
   251→            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
   252→                resp = await client.get("http://localhost:8000/health")
   253→                surreal_healthy = resp.status_code == 200
   254→        except Exception:
   255→            surreal_healthy = False
   256→
   257→        status = self.detector.check("surrealdb", "available", 1.0 if surreal_healthy else 0.0, 0.1)
   258→        if status.status != "healthy":
   259→            issues.append(status)
   260→
   261→        # Check sandbox health via ResourceMonitor
   262→        try:
   263→            from cohezion.reliability.monitor import get_resource_monitor
   264→
   265→            monitor = get_resource_monitor()
   266→            sandbox_mem = monitor.total_sandbox_memory_mb
   267→            # Flag if sandboxes are using >80GB (80% of 100GB budget)
   268→            sandbox_ratio = sandbox_mem / (100 * 1024) if sandbox_mem > 0 else 0.0
   269→            status = self.detector.check("sandbox", "memory_pressure", sandbox_ratio, 0.8)
   270→            if status.status != "healthy":
   271→                issues.append(status)
   272→        except Exception as e:
   273→            logger.debug("Sandbox memory check failed: %s", e)
   274→
   275→        return issues
   276→
   277→    async def heal(self, issues: list[HealthStatus]) -> int:
   278→        """Attempt to heal detected issues."""
   279→        healed = 0
   280→
   281→        for issue in issues:
   282→            diagnosis = self.diagnostician.diagnose(issue)
   283→            if diagnosis.confidence >= 0.5 and await self.corrector.apply_correction(diagnosis):
   284→                healed += 1
   285→                logger.info(f"Healed: {diagnosis.issue}")
   286→
   287→        return healed
   288→
   289→
   290→# Singleton
   291→_system: SelfHealingSystem | None = None
   292→
   293→
   294→def get_healing_system() -> SelfHealingSystem:
   295→    global _system
   296→    if _system is None:
   297→        _system = SelfHealingSystem()
   298→    return _system

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Wiring healing/ → DegradationDetector**: The healing module has 3 complementary layers: `DriftDetector` (baselines + drift %), `Diagnostician` (pattern-match to known issues), and `Corrector` (apply fixes). The DegradationDetector already does statistical anomaly detection on 5 metrics. The wire connects them as a **two-stage pipeline**: DegradationDetector fires alerts → healing's Diagnostician classifies root cause → Corrector attempts auto-fix. This is the MAPE-K pattern (Monitor→Analyze→Plan→Execute) applied to the compound loop.

**Key design choice**: Wire as a non-blocking post-check in DegradationDetector, not by merging the modules. This preserves both modules' independence and follows the Hookify philosophy of integration glue.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

   144→        if health_status.metric == "quality_score" and health_status.status in (
   145→            "degraded",
   146→            "failing",
   147→        ):
   148→            return self._known_issues["low_quality"]
   149→
   150→        if health_status.component == "ollama" and health_status.status == "failing":
   151→            return self._known_issues["connection_failed"]
   152→
   153→        if health_status.component == "sandbox" and health_status.metric == "divergence":
   154→            return self._known_issues["sandbox_divergence"]
   155→
   156→        # Generic diagnosis
   157→        return DiagnosisResult(
   158→            component=health_status.component,
   159→            issue=f"{health_status.metric} {health_status.status}",
   160→            probable_cause="Unknown - requires investigation",
   161→            recommended_action="Check logs and component health",
   162→            confidence=0.3,
   163→        )
   164→
   165→
   166→class Corrector:
   167→    """Autonomous correction of detected issues."""
   168→
   169→    def __init__(self):
   170→        self._corrections: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   171→
   172→    async def apply_correction(self, diagnosis: DiagnosisResult) -> bool:
   173→        """Apply automatic correction based on diagnosis."""
   174→        correction = {
   175→            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
   176→            "component": diagnosis.component,
   177→            "issue": diagnosis.issue,
   178→            "action": diagnosis.recommended_action,
   179→            "applied": False,
   180→        }
   181→
   182→        # Auto-corrections we can apply
   183→        if "swap model" in diagnosis.recommended_action.lower():
   184→            # Trigger model manager to benchmark and swap
   185→            from cohezion.swarm.model_manager import get_manager
   186→
   187→            get_manager()
   188→            # Mark as needing swap - actual swap happens on next call
   189→            correction["applied"] = True
   190→            logger.info(f"Scheduled model swap for {diagnosis.component}")
   191→
   192→        self._corrections.append(correction)
   193→        self._save_log()
   194→
   195→        return correction["applied"]
   196→
   197→    def _save_log(self) -> None:
   198→        """Save correction history."""
   199→        HEALTH_LOG_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   200→        HEALTH_LOG_PATH.write_text(
   201→            json.dumps(
   202→                {
   203→                    "corrections": self._corrections[-100:],
   204→                },
   205→                indent=2,
   206→            )
   207→        )
   208→
   209→    def get_history(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   210→        """Get correction history."""
   211→        return self._corrections
   212→
   213→
   214→class SelfHealingSystem:
   215→    """
   216→    Complete self-healing system.
   217→
   218→    Integrates:
   219→    - Drift detection
   220→    - LLM-based diagnosis
   221→    - Autonomous correction
   222→    """
   223→
   224→    def __init__(self):
   225→        self.detector = DriftDetector()
   226→        self.diagnostician = Diagnostician()
   227→        self.corrector = Corrector()
   228→
   229→    async def health_check(self) -> list[HealthStatus]:
   230→        """Run full system health check."""
   231→        issues = []
   232→
   233→        # Check Ollama
   234→        try:
   235→            import httpx
   236→
   237→            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
   238→                resp = await client.get("http://localhost:11434/api/tags")
   239→                ollama_healthy = resp.status_code == 200
   240→        except Exception:
   241→            ollama_healthy = False
   242→
   243→        status = self.detector.check("ollama", "available", 1.0 if ollama_healthy else 0.0, 0.1)
   244→        if status.status != "healthy":
   245→            issues.append(status)
   246→
   247→        # Check SurrealDB
   248→        try:
   249→            import httpx
   250→
   251→            async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
   252→                resp = await client.get("http://localhost:8000/health")
   253→                surreal_healthy = resp.status_code == 200
   254→        except Exception:
   255→            surreal_healthy = False
   256→
   257→        status = self.detector.check("surrealdb", "available", 1.0 if surreal_healthy else 0.0, 0.1)
   258→        if status.status != "healthy":
   259→            issues.append(status)
   260→
   261→        # Check sandbox health via ResourceMonitor
   262→        try:
   263→            from cohezion.reliability.monitor import get_resource_monitor
   264→
   265→            monitor = get_resource_monitor()
   266→            sandbox_mem = monitor.total_sandbox_memory_mb
   267→            # Flag if sandboxes are using >80GB (80% of 100GB budget)
   268→            sandbox_ratio = sandbox_mem / (100 * 1024) if sandbox_mem > 0 else 0.0
   269→            status = self.detector.check("sandbox", "memory_pressure", sandbox_ratio, 0.8)
   270→            if status.status != "healthy":
   271→                issues.append(status)
   272→        except Exception as e:
   273→            logger.debug("Sandbox memory check failed: %s", e)
   274→
   275→        return issues
   276→
   277→    async def heal(self, issues: list[HealthStatus]) -> int:
   278→        """Attempt to heal detected issues."""
   279→        healed = 0
   280→
   281→        for issue in issues:
   282→            diagnosis = self.diagnostician.diagnose(issue)
   283→            if diagnosis.confidence >= 0.5 and await self.corrector.apply_correction(diagnosis):
   284→                healed += 1
   285→                logger.info(f"Healed: {diagnosis.issue}")
   286→
   287→        return healed
   288→
   289→
   290→# Singleton
   291→_system: SelfHealingSystem | None = None
   292→
   293→
   294→def get_healing_system() -> SelfHealingSystem:
   295→    global _system
   296→    if _system is None:
   297→        _system = SelfHealingSystem()
   298→    return _system
   299→

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**eval/ vs evaluation/ consolidation**: `eval/` has 3 substantial modules (capability_scorecard, pipeline, huggingface_export) while `evaluation/` has just 1 (self_eval with ~54 lines of pre-flight checks). The SelfEvaluationEngine fits naturally as a pre-execution gate in the compound pipeline. Rather than merging directories, I'll wire both into their natural integration points:
- **CapabilityScorecard** → CapabilityMatrix (provides EVO-specific 6-axis metrics)
- **SelfEvaluationEngine** → CompoundExecutor (pre-flight quality gate before execution)

   260→    def recommend_for_task(
   261→        self,
   262→        task_type: str,
   263→        constraints: dict | None = None,
   264→    ) -> list[CapabilityEntry]:
   265→        """Recommend entities for a task type, sorted by affinity score."""
   266→        constraints = constraints or {}
   267→        max_latency = constraints.get("max_latency_ms", float("inf"))
   268→        min_quality = constraints.get("min_quality", 0.0)
   269→        entity_types = constraints.get("entity_types", ["model"])
   270→
   271→        candidates = []
   272→        for entry in self._entries.values():
   273→            if entry.entity_type not in entity_types:

   276→                continue
   277→            latency = entry.metadata.get("latency_ms", 0.0)
   278→            if latency > max_latency:
   279→                continue
   280→            affinity = entry.affinity.get(task_type, 0.0)
   281→            candidates.append((affinity + entry.quality_score, entry))
   282→
   283→        candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
   284→        return [entry for _, entry in candidates]

   306→                gaps.append(gap)

   308→        return gaps

   371→                entry.success_rate = (old_successes + (1.0 if success else 0.0)) / total
   372→                entry.metadata["invocations"] = total

   281→### Learning 219: Data Mesh × MCP Registry (2026-03-31)
   282→17+ MCP servers = 17 data domains. DataProduct type with schema, SLA, lineage, and ownership turns tools into governed data products. Factory pattern (get_cohezion_data_products()) prevents shared mutable state. MCP Registry is the self-serve platform layer of Data Mesh.

   284→### Learning 220: A2UI Makes Agent Testing Structural (2026-03-31)
   285→Component catalog (JSON) + experience scripts replace opaque WebGL testing. Agent validates the data structure, not the pixels. 9 Playwright e2e tests + 26 pytest tests. Data-attribute selectors (data-a2ui-component) are the most reliable Playwright selectors for dynamic UIs.
   286→### Learning 221: LeWM — Missing JEPA World Model Upgrade (2026-03-31)
   287→lucas-maes/le-wm is the first stable end-to-end JEPA from raw pixels using only 2 loss terms (next-embedding prediction + Gaussian regularizer). 15M params, single GPU, trains in hours, plans 48x faster than foundation models. Latent space encodes physical structure and detects implausible events. Direct upgrade path for Cohezion's 86K-param JEPAWorldModel.      2→
     3→## DOMAIN EXPERTISE
     4→You are a Staff Security and Reliability Engineer focused on preventing systemic illusions, configuration drift, and silent failures within the FLUME/Ollama architecture.
     5→
     6→## KEY TEXTS & CONCEPTS
     7→* **The Sudo Trap:** Relying on elevated privileges to read hardware states when `sysfs` provides user-space truth.
     8→* **GTT Carveout Illusion:** Misinterpreting unified memory allocations (GTT) as VRAM exhaustion, causing false out-of-memory panics.
     9→* **Scope Collision:** Modifying the wrong configuration file due to naming similarities (e.g., `~/.claude.json` vs `~/.claude/mcp.json`).
    10→* **Silent Auth Drift:** Allowing the system to gracefully fall back to in-memory stores when primary SurrealDB authentication fails, masking the critical infrastructure failure.
    11→
    12→## INSTRUCTION
    13→1. **Hardware Verification:** Always read directly from `/sys/class/drm/` or vendor-agnostic sysfs paths for GPU memory. Never assume `nvidia-smi` or `rocm-smi` wrappers are reporting the full unified memory picture on APUs.
    14→2. **Config Path Hardening:** Explicitly verify the target application's documented config path before injecting MCPs or settings.
    15→3. **Fail-Fast Persistence:** If SurrealDB `UPSERT` fails due to `InvalidAuth`, the system MUST log a `CRITICAL` error and halt the specific agent loop rather than silently falling back to `InMemoryStore`.
    16→4. **Halt on Import Shadows:** Enforce strict `# noqa: E402` or delayed imports during patching. If an import fails, crash immediately instead of catching and passing.
    17→
    18→## VERSION
    19→v1.0.1

Fix: direct sysfs GPU/VRAM monitoring, aggressive PID kill in RED alert, `tune_system.sh` to disable panic-on-oom, prevention of giant coredumps. Key insight: **VRAM is the bottleneck, not RAM. Swarms must be sacrificial; system integrity is primary.**
    50→
    51→### Learning 105: The Untrack & Mine Protocol
    52→Operational procedure invented during ops/hygiene: (1) identify tracked files that shouldn't be, (2) mine them for knowledge before removal, (3) add to .gitignore, (4) `git rm --cached`, (5) verify git status clean. Critical rule: NEVER delete without reading first. This protocol prevented knowledge loss during the 8.6M file cleanup.

This validates our vault-first approach and suggests we should expose execution traces as browsable files, not prompt context.

## Comprehensive Exploration Report: Governance & Routing Upgrade Research

Based on systematic exploration of the Cohezion codebase, here are my findings organized by the three research areas:

---

### 1. LAYERED GOVERNANCE ARCHITECTURE (L1-L4) — Current Implementation

#### What Exists Today

**L1: Constitutional Enforcement**
- **File**: `src/cohezion/validation/constitutional.py` (86 lines)
- **Current State**: Skeleton implementation with mock teacher model
  - `ConstitutionalShield` class audits agent outputs against CONSTITUTION.md and COHEZION_CHARTER.md
  - `audit_output()` returns mock alignment score (0.95) with verdict "Clear"
  - `ManifoldEquilibrium` validates topological stability using HIHO 0.5 attractor rule
  - **Gap**: Uses mock CAI feedback loop; doesn't actually invoke teacher model for critique
  - **Logging**: Attempts to log audits to SurrealDB via `self.db.create("constitutional_audit", analysis)`

**L2: Request-Level Intent Verification**
- **File**: `src/cohezion/compound/request_alignment_analyzer.py` (963 lines — comprehensive)
- **Current State**: Full implementation with vault integration
  - Parses raw requests into structured `HumanRequest` (intent, constraints, criteria)
  - Classifies intent via keyword matching + semantic fallback (lazy-loaded encoder)
  - Extracts constraints (tokens, latency, quality, scope) using regex patterns
  - Extracts success criteria from explicit "must/should" statements
  - Computes `ExecutionAlignment` (intent match, constraint satisfaction, criteria satisfaction, drift signals)
  - **Misalignment scoring**: Composite = 0.4×intent + 0.3×constraints + 0.3×criteria, penalized by drift
  - **Vault integration**: High misalignment (>0.5) logged as decision (ADR); normal logged as experiment
  - **Pattern querying**: `query_alignment_patterns()` fetches prior misalignments via vault

**L2.5: Guardrail Pipeline**
- **File**: `src/cohezion/security/guardrail_pipeline.py` (262 lines)
- **Current State**: Protocol-driven orchestrator
  - Composable guardrail pipeline with short-circuit logic
  - Execution order: ConstitutionalShield → PromptGuard → ResourceGuard → RateLimitGuard → OutputFilter
  - Actions: ALLOW, BLOCK, SANITIZE, LOG_AND_ALLOW
  - Non-blocking audit callback
  - Statistics tracking (allowed/blocked/sanitized per guardrail)
  - **Gap**: Assumes guardrail implementations exist; only defines protocol and orchestration

**L3: Execution-Time Behavior Monitoring**
- **Files**: 
  - `src/cohezion/compound/degradation_detector.py` (375 lines)
  - `src/cohezion/compound/journey_tracker.py` (300+ lines)
  - `src/cohezion/compound/inflection_detector.py` (385 lines)
- **Degradation Detector** monitors:
  - Cache hit rate (alert <50%)
  - Token efficiency (alert >10% drop from baseline)
  - Coherence (alert <0.6)
  - Duration slowdown (alert >25% increase)
  - Healing pipeline integration (non-blocking)
- **Journey Tracker** captures:
  - 12D FLUME trajectories from execution metrics
  - Operation-specific modulation profiles (GENERATE, ANALYZE, SEARCH, TRANSFORM, PERSIST)
  - Trajectory quality score (coherence×0.5 + smoothness×0.3 + convergence×0.2)
  - Persists `TrajectoryPoint` and `Journey` for experience guidance
- **Inflection Detector** detects anomalies (severity: INFO, WARNING, CRITICAL)

**L4: Persistent Audit Trail & Experience Replay**
- **Files**:
  - `src/cohezion/compound/exp_persistence/vault.py` (198 lines)
  - `src/cohezion/governance/knowledge_bridge.py` (120+ lines)
  - `src/cohezion/compound/executor.py` (150+ lines shown)
- **VaultLogger** implements:
  - `log_execution_start()` → experiments/{project}/{skill}/{timestamp}.json
  - `log_execution_result()` → updates with success, output_summary, metrics, end_time
  - `get_experience_guidance()` → queries vault for similar patterns
  - `extract_execution_pattern()` → saves reusable patterns to patterns/domains/{domain}/
  - `log_decision_point()` → critical decisions to decisions/{project}/inflection_{timestamp}.md
  - `log_batch()` → importance-sampled mission retrospectives to vault
- **KnowledgeBridge** provides:
  - Bidirectional persistence: Obsidian vault + SurrealDB + KEY_LEARNINGS.md
  - Learning dataclass with number, title, content, date, tags, propagate_to, links
  - `persist_to_vault()` writes dated markdown with YAML frontmatter + [[bidirectional links]]
  - `persist_to_surrealdb()` inserts with FLUME embedding (base64-encoded)

#### The Gaps (Research Targets)

1. **Missing L1 Tier Enforcement**: ConstitutionalShield doesn't block requests; it only audits with mock scores. No actual teacher model critique or hard rejection.

2. **No Execution Traces Directory**: VaultLogger logs to `experiments/{project}/{skill}/{timestamp}.json` but there's no centralized `execution_traces/` directory for meta-analysis.

3. **RequestAlignmentAnalyzer is Pre-Execution Only**: It doesn't integrate post-execution for closed-loop alignment checking. Misalignment detection is one-way (request → plan, but not result validation).

4. **Inflection Detector is Separate from RequestAlignmentAnalyzer**: Anomalies are detected independently; they don't feed back into request coherence scoring.

5. **No OI-MAS Confidence Propagation**: The 4-layer architecture doesn't propagate confidence scores upward. An L3 anomaly doesn't reduce L2 constraint satisfaction; they're independent signals.

6. **Knowledge Bridge is Write-Only from Retrospection**: The knowledge bridge persists learnings but doesn't pull them into live execution to adjust thresholds dynamically.

### 2. OI-MAS CONFIDENCE-AWARE ROUTING — Current Implementation

#### What Exists Today

**Model Selection & Routing Infrastructure**
- **Files**:
  - `src/cohezion/swarm/smart_router.py` (500+ lines)
  - `src/cohezion/swarm/cost_aware_router.py` (600+ lines)
  - `src/cohezion/swarm/dynamic_model_router.py` (700+ lines)
  - `src/cohezion/swarm/tip_of_spear_router.py` (500+ lines)
  - `src/cohezion/swarm/topological_router.py` (600+ lines)

**SmartRouter** defines:
- TaskType enum: ANALYSIS, SYNTHESIS, CREATIVE, CODING, FACTUAL, DEBATE, SUMMARY
- ModelCapability enum: FAST, ACCURATE, CREATIVE, LARGE_CONTEXT, CODING
- ModelProfile dataclass with name, capabilities, context_length, speed_tier, quality_tier
- LOCAL_MODELS dictionary with 15+ models (qwen3-coder-next, phi4, deepseek-r1, etc.)
- Efficiency score = quality_tier / speed_tier

**CostAwareRouter** provides:
- QueryComplexity tiers: SIMPLE, MEDIUM, COMPLEX
- QueryComplexityAnalyzer with keyword-based analysis (SIMPLE_KEYWORDS, COMPLEX_KEYWORDS)
- Token estimation via `_estimate_tokens(query)` (rough heuristic)
- ModelRoutingDecision dataclass (model, complexity, estimated_tokens, estimated_cost_usd, reason, quality_score)
- RoutingStatistics (total_queries, simple/medium/complex counts, model routing distributions, total_cost_usd, cost savings vs. deepseek-only)
- Integration with BudgetEnforcer for hard budget stops
- Integration with SessionCostTracker for usage tracking

**TipOfTheSpearRouter** provides:
- ConstitutionalChecker with hard line keyword detection (WMD, CRITICAL_INFRA, MALICIOUS_CODE, CSAM, etc.)
- ModelTier escalation chain: HOT → WARM → COLD → CLOUD
- ConstitutionalViolation enum (7 violation types)
- SovereigntyCheckResult (constitutional_compliant, violation, ethical_score, hiho_stability, requires_human_review, warnings)
- RoutingResult with confidence, escalation_count, sovereignty_metadata, idempotency_key
- **Confidence-based escalation**: If confidence <0.7, escalate to next tier (but escalation logic is sketched, not fully implemented)

**DynamicModelRouter** (700 lines):
- Detects available models at runtime via Ollama
- Enforces global concurrency limit of 4 (Ollama constraint)
- Health monitoring per model (latency, error rates, token efficiency)
- Fallback strategies on model failures
- Load balancing across available models

#### Current Gaps

1. **No True OI-MAS Integration**: The routing system doesn't use confidence scores to modulate task decomposition. All routing is task-first (classify task → select model), not confidence-first.

2. **Confidence Scoring is Incomplete**: `ModelRoutingDecision.quality_score` exists but isn't used to gate escalation. `TipOfTheSpearRouter.route_with_sovereignty()` mentions confidence <0.7 escalation but the full implementation is missing.

3. **No Task Type Detection at Execution Time**: Routing happens once at start; it doesn't adapt as execution unfolds. An initially SIMPLE query that encounters anomalies doesn't trigger re-routing.

4. **No Bidirectional Confidence Flow**: Execution confidence doesn't flow back to adjust model selection. Model A fails with 0.2 confidence → next time, skip model A, not "Model A escalates to Model B."

5. **Cost-Aware Routing Doesn't Consider Confidence**: CostAwareRouter minimizes cost without considering whether the cheap model will succeed. No confidence threshold enforcement.

6. **Topological Router Exists But Isn't Wired**: `topological_router.py` uses persistent homology (TDA) to classify behavior into exploit/explore/pivot regimes, but it's not integrated into the main routing pipeline.

#### The Wiring Points

- **ExecutionOrchestrator** (`src/cohezion/swarm/execution_orchestrator.py`) is the proposed integration point
- **TeamOrchestrator** (`src/cohezion/swarm/team_orchestrator.py`) handles multi-agent coordination but doesn't route based on confidence

### 3. EXECUTION TRACES & META-HARNESS PATTERN — Current Implementation

#### What Exists Today

**Execution Persistence Architecture**
- **Primary logging**: VaultLogger (vault.py) logs to `experiments/{project}/{skill}/{timestamp}.json`
- **Decision logging**: `log_decision_point()` → `decisions/{project}/inflection_{timestamp}.md`
- **Pattern extraction**: `extract_execution_pattern()` → `patterns/domains/{domain}/{pattern_name}.md`
- **Mission retrospectives**: `log_batch()` → `missions/{mission_id}.md` with importance sampling

**Execution Lifecycle in CompoundExecutor** (`executor.py`):
1. Query vault for experience guidance
2. Execute task with token-efficient client
3. Logs are persisted to vault automatically via VaultLogger
4. Extract patterns for future use
5. Skill refinement from execution results

**Skill Learning from Execution** (`skill_refiner.py`):
- Extracts ExecutionMetrics (success, duration, tokens_used, token_efficiency, quality_score, anomaly_score, cached_hits)
- Generates LearningSignal (skill_name, operation_type, key_insight, metric_change, recommendation, confidence)
- Appends refinement to PRIME .md file (updates version)
- Persists to vault + SurrealDB via KnowledgeBridge (non-blocking)

**Autonomy Tier System** (`governance/autonomy_engine.py`):
- Maps cosmogonic chain to autonomy tiers: VOID → SO(12) → SO(3)⁴ → U(1)⁴ → Z₂⁴ → HIHO
- Coherence thresholds: 0.0 (VOID), 0.2 (SO12), 0.35 (SO3⁴), 0.45 (U1⁴), 0.48 (Z2⁴), 0.50 (HIHO)
- Promotion requires 5 consecutive checks above threshold
- Demotion triggers on 3 consecutive failures
- Tracks `AgentAutonomyState` (agent_id, current_tier, coherence_history, tier_transitions, created_at, last_check)

**Session Concierge** (`governance/concierge.py`):
- Gathers SessionBriefing from 7 state sources (branch, worktree count, continuation task, active plans, recent commits, SurrealDB health, vault entries)
- Generates RoutingSuggestion (action, target, confidence, reason, autonomy_tier)
- Learns from routing history (JSONL file at `~/.cohezion-engine/routing_history.jsonl`)
- Semantic routing via FLUME bridge (if available)
- HIHO governance: confidence >0.8 = strong match, ~0.5 = present options, <0.3 = fresh start

#### Current Gaps

1. **No Centralized execution_traces/ Directory**: Traces are scattered across experiments/, decisions/, patterns/, missions/. No unified query interface.

2. **No Execution Trace Versioning**: If the same skill runs twice, both logs go to different files (timestamped). No parent-child relationship between runs.

3. **No Meta-Harness Implementation**: There's no system to:
   - Collect all execution traces
   - Analyze patterns across 100+ executions
   - Detect systematic failures
   - Recommend structural changes (vs. parameter tuning)

4. **No Backward-Flow from Meta-Analysis**: Degradation alerts are detected but don't trigger meta-harness analysis. No automatic pivot protocol.

5. **Inflection Detector Doesn't Output Structured Traces**: Anomalies are logged to logger, not persisted as traceable artifacts.

6. **No Execution Sequence Tracking**: Each execution is independent. No tracking of task sequences, intermediate results, or backtracking patterns.

| **L4: Knowledge Bridge** | `governance/knowledge_bridge.py` | 120+ | Learning, persist_to_vault, persist_to_surrealdb | Write-only; learnings don't feed back |
| **Routing: Smart** | `swarm/smart_router.py` | 500+ | SmartRouter, ModelProfile, TaskType, ModelCapability | Task-first routing; no confidence modulation |
| **Routing: Cost** | `swarm/cost_aware_router.py` | 600+ | CostAwareRouter, QueryComplexityAnalyzer, ModelRoutingDecision | Minimizes cost, ignores confidence |
| **Routing: Tip-of-Spear** | `swarm/tip_of_spear_router.py` | 500+ | TipOfTheSpearRouter, ConstitutionalChecker, ModelTier | Escalation sketched; not fully wired |
| **Routing: Dynamic** | `swarm/dynamic_model_router.py` | 700+ | DynamicModelRouter, ModelHealth, HealthMonitor | Runtime model detection; no confidence feedback |
| **Routing: Topological** | `swarm/topological_router.py` | 600+ | TopologicalRouter, BehaviorRegime (exploit/explore/pivot) | Detects regimes but not integrated into main routing |
| **Execution** | `compound/executor.py` | 150+ shown | CompoundExecutor, ExecutionResult | No post-execution alignment check |
| **Skill Learning** | `compound/skill_refiner.py` | 300+ | SkillRefiner, LearningSignal, ExecutionMetrics | Appends to PRIME; doesn't update thresholds |
| **Autonomy** | `governance/autonomy_engine.py` | 200+ | AutonomyEngine, AgentAutonomyState, AutonomyTier | Tier tracking; not wired to routing decisions |
| **Concierge** | `governance/concierge.py` | 350+ | ConciergeAgent, SessionBriefing, RoutingSuggestion | Session routing only; doesn't handle task confidence |

---

### 5. Critical Insights for Implementation

#### Architecture Observations

1. **Four Separate Routing Systems Exist**:
   - SmartRouter (task → capability matching)
   - CostAwareRouter (complexity → model)
   - TipOfTheSpearRouter (constitutional → escalation chain)
   - DynamicModelRouter (runtime health → fallback)
   - **None integrate with each other or with request-level confidence.**

2. **L2 (Request Alignment) is Comprehensive but Isolated**:
   - Parses requests deeply (intent, constraints, criteria, scope, drift signals)
   - Computes misalignment scores
   - Logs to vault
   - **But**: Never consulted during execution routing. ExecutionOrchestrator doesn't call RequestAlignmentAnalyzer to gate model selection.

3. **L3 (Behavior Monitoring) Detects But Doesn't Decide**:
   - DegradationDetector alerts on cache/token/coherence drops
   - JourneyTracker records 12D trajectories
   - InflectionDetector finds anomalies
   - **But**: None of these trigger routing changes. An execution with 0.3 coherence still routed the same as 0.9.

4. **L4 (Audit Trail) is Well-Designed but Backward-Only**:
   - VaultLogger logs execution results
   - KnowledgeBridge persists learnings
   - SkillRefiner updates PRIME files
   - **But**: These learnings don't feed back into L1-L3 thresholds. A skill with 50% recent success rate still used at same priority.

5. **Autonomy Tiers Exist But Aren't Governance Levels**:
   - AutonomyEngine tracks coherence history → tier transitions
   - **But**: Tiers only control agent privileges (VOID = no access, HIHO = full), not task difficulty routing or confidence thresholds.

#### Data Flow Observations

- **Forward Flow (Request → Execution)**: Well-wired (request → smart router → model selection → execute)
- **Execution Flow (Runtime)**: Partially monitored (degradation alerts, journey tracking exist but isolated)
- **Backward Flow (Result → Decision Adjustment)**: Missing
  - Execution results stored in vault
  - Learnings extracted
  - PRIME skills updated
  - **But no loop back to L1-L2 thresholds, model selection weights, or routing confidence gates**

---

### 6. Recommended Integration Points for Research Implementation

1. **Unify Execution Traces**:
   - Central `execution_traces/` directory
   - Parent-child tracking (task → subtasks → executions)
   - Queryable index by skill, operation_type, success, confidence

2. **Wire Request Alignment → Routing**:
   - ExecutionOrchestrator calls RequestAlignmentAnalyzer before execution
   - If misalignment_score >0.5, gate execution or escalate tier
   - Store alignment analysis in execution trace

3. **Propagate L3 Anomalies → L2 Confidence**:
   - If degradation_detector alerts, reduce model tier selection confidence
   - If journey coherence <0.5, mark as "experimental" in next run

4. **Implement Meta-Harness**:
   - Query execution_traces/ for patterns across 100+ runs
   - Detect systematic failures vs. noise
   - Output pivot recommendations (architectural change needed)

5. **Create Backward-Flow Multiplier**:
   - Track skill success rates in window (last 10 executions)
   - Reduce model quality tier if success rate <0.6
   - Track per-agent coherence → autonomy tier transitions

6. **Integrate Topological Router**:
   - Use TDA behavior regime classification (exploit/explore/pivot)
   - Route EXPLORE tasks to diverse model tier
   - Route EXPLOIT tasks to proven model

---

This exploration provides the foundation for the three-phase upgrade research. The Cohezion codebase has all the components; they just need to be wired together with confidence-aware routing and closed-loop feedback.

## Session 82 Implementation Plan: Compound Loop Module Wiring (Phase 2)

### Executive Summary

Session 81 wired 4 orphaned modules (healing/, resilience/, eval/, evaluation/) into the compound loop using the non-blocking try/except pattern in `DegradationDetector.check_degradation()`. Session 82 continues this work across 3 phases with 8 tasks, wiring the remaining disconnected modules into the compound execution pipeline.

### Key Architecture Insight: Compound Value Ordering

The optimal ordering is not Phase 1 -> 2 -> 3 sequentially. Instead, the routing feedback loop (Phase 3, Item 7) should be elevated to Phase 1 because it **unlocks compound value for every subsequent task** -- once DegradationDetector alerts flow back to CostAwareRouter, all future execution automatically benefits from adaptive routing. The quick wins (Items 1-3) are purely additive and can be done in any order.

Recommended execution order:
1. **Task 1: R-Zero -> CostAwareRouter** (Phase 1, unlocks model selection improvement for all tasks)
2. **Task 2: DegradationDetector -> CostAwareRouter feedback** (Phase 3, high-impact routing loop)
3. **Task 3: SwarmEnv gym.register** (Phase 1, zero-dependency quick win)
4. **Task 4: NightlyReporter -> configurable path** (Phase 1, quick win)
5. **Task 5: BioelectricNetwork -> JourneyTracker + DegradationDetector** (Phase 2)
6. **Task 6: NaturalCapitalValuation -> CompoundExecutor reward** (Phase 2)
7. **Task 7: JEPA auto-train on first ManifoldEnv episode** (Phase 2)
8. **Task 8: Execution traces directory** (Phase 3)

### Task 1: Wire R-Zero Optimization to CostAwareRouter

**Goal:** LocalModelOptimizer's success rate history informs CostAwareRouter model quality scores.

**Files to modify:**
- `/home/mike-anderson/dev/cohezion/src/cohezion/swarm/cost_aware_router.py`

  - Add `_apply_r_zero_adjustment()` method: queries `LocalModelOptimizer.get_current_multiplier()` and applies it to `MODEL_QUALITY` scores for local models. When multiplier is 0.8 (success rate < 80%), reduce quality scores for local models by 20%.

- `/home/mike-anderson/dev/cohezion/src/cohezion/optimization/r_zero.py`

### Dependencies and Sequencing

```
Task 1 (R-Zero -> Router) ──────────────────────┐
Task 2 (Degradation -> Router Feedback) ─────────┤── Both improve routing quality
Task 3 (SwarmEnv register) ──────────────────────┤── Independent
Task 4 (NightlyReporter) ───────────────────────┤── Independent
                                                  │
Task 5 (Bioelectric -> Journey + Degradation) ───┤── Benefits from Task 2 feedback loop
Task 6 (NaturalCapital -> Executor) ─────────────┤── Independent, enriches coherence
Task 7 (JEPA auto-train) ───────────────────────┤── Benefits from Task 5 (richer journey)
                                                  │
Task 8 (Execution traces) ──────────────────────┘── Benefits from all above (richer data)
```

Tasks 1-4 are independent and can be parallelized. Tasks 5-7 can also be parallelized. Task 8 depends on Tasks 1-7 being complete for maximum trace richness.

# Session 82: Compound Loop Wiring Phase 2 + Routing Feedback

## Context
Session 81 wired 4 orphaned modules (healing/, resilience/, eval/, evaluation/) into the compound loop, extracted L225-L229, and created 4 PRIME skills. External research confirmed architecture decisions and identified high-priority integration candidates (IsoQuant, OI-MAS, Layered Governance, V-JEPA 2.1).

**Problem**: 6+ modules remain orphaned or partially connected. Four routing systems (SmartRouter, CostAwareRouter, TipOfTheSpearRouter, DynamicModelRouter) operate independently without confidence feedback. Execution results don't flow backward to adjust future routing.

**Outcome**: Close the backward feedback loop (L3 alerts → routing adjustment), wire remaining physics/world-model modules, and implement execution traces (Meta-Harness L225 pattern).

## Prior Work (Sessions 80-81)
- Session 80: 17 commits — GeminiProvider, C1-C5 token efficiency, knowledge bridge, A2A cards
- Session 81: 4 modules wired (healing→Degradation, resilience→Degradation, eval→CapabilityMatrix, evaluation→CapabilityMatrix), L225-L229 extracted, 4 PRIME skills created
- 1064 compound tests passing (9 pre-existing FLUME failures)

     5→import logging

     7→from pydantic import BaseModel
     8→
     9→
    10→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    11→
    12→
    13→class RZeroMetrics(BaseModel):
    14→    """Track metrics for compound engineering success rates."""
    15→
    16→    success_rate: float
    17→    iteration_count: int
    18→    difficulty_adjustment: float
    19→
    20→
    21→class LocalModelOptimizer:
    22→    """Connects R-Zero metrics to local Ollama models (Qwen3-Coder, DeepSeek-R1)."""
    23→
    24→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    25→        self.metrics_history: list[RZeroMetrics] = []
    26→
    27→    def record_execution(self, model_name: str, success: bool, iterations: int) -> None:
    28→        """Record the execution pass of a local model."""
    29→        # Calculate trailing success rate
    30→        recent_successes = sum(1 for m in self.metrics_history[-10:] if m.success_rate == 1.0)
    31→        total = min(10, max(1, len(self.metrics_history)))
    32→
    33→        base_rate = (recent_successes + (1 if success else 0)) / (total + 1)
    34→
    35→        metrics = RZeroMetrics(
    36→            success_rate=base_rate,
    37→            iteration_count=iterations,
    38→            difficulty_adjustment=1.0 if base_rate > 0.8 else 0.8,
    39→        )
    40→        self.metrics_history.append(metrics)
    41→        logger.info(
    42→            f"R-Zero metrics updated for {model_name}: SR={base_rate:.2f}, Iter={iterations}"
    43→        )
    44→
    45→    def get_current_multiplier(self) -> float:
    46→        """Get the current difficulty multiplier based on R-Zero metrics."""
    47→        if not self.metrics_history:
    48→            return 1.0
    49→        return self.metrics_history[-1].difficulty_adjustment
    50→

     9→  POST /world-model/train        — Train on synthetic or stored data
    10→  POST /world-model/predict      — Predict next state from current + action
    11→  POST /world-model/simulate     — Roll out N-step trajectory

    38→        return self._mcp

    40→    # ── VaultExecutionLogger Contract ──────────────────────────────────
    41→
    42→    def log_execution_start(self, ctx: ExecutionContext) -> str:
    43→        """Log the start of an execution to the Vault."""
    44→        try:
    45→            path = (
    46→                f"experiments/{ctx.project}/{ctx.skill_name}/{int(ctx.start_time.timestamp())}.json"
    47→            )
    48→            data = {
    49→                "project": ctx.project,
    50→                "skill_name": ctx.skill_name,
    51→                "task_description": ctx.task_description,
    52→                "operation_type": ctx.operation_type,
    53→                "start_time": ctx.start_time.isoformat(),
    54→                "status": "started",
    55→            }
    56→            self.mcp.vault_write(path, json.dumps(data, indent=2))
    57→            return path
    58→        except Exception as e:
    59→            logger.error(f"Failed to log execution start to Vault: {e}")
    60→            return ""
    61→
    62→    def log_execution_result(
    63→        self, experiment_path: str, success: bool, output: str, metrics: dict[str, Any]
    64→    ):
    65→        """Update the execution log with results."""
    66→        if not experiment_path:
    67→            return
    68→        try:
    69→            # Read existing
    70→            content = self.mcp.vault_read(experiment_path)
    71→            data = json.loads(content)
    72→
    73→            # Update
    74→            data["success"] = success
    75→            data["output_summary"] = output[:1000] if output else ""
    76→            data["metrics"] = metrics
    77→            data["status"] = "completed"
    78→            data["end_time"] = datetime.now().isoformat()
    79→
    80→            self.mcp.vault_write(experiment_path, json.dumps(data, indent=2))
    81→        except Exception as e:
    82→            logger.error(f"Failed to log execution result to Vault: {e}")
    83→
    84→    def get_experience_guidance(
    85→        self, task_description: str, project: str = "cohezion"
    86→    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    87→        """Fetch similar patterns from the Vault for guidance."""
    88→        try:
    89→            # Simple keyword extraction for search
    90→            keywords = [w for w in task_description.lower().split() if len(w) > 4][:3]
    91→            query = " ".join(keywords) if keywords else "general"
    92→
    93→            logger.debug(f"Searching Vault for guidance: {query}")
    94→            patterns = self.mcp.vault_search(query)
    95→
    96→            return {
    97→                "relevant_context": patterns,
    98→                "guidance": f"Retrieved {len(patterns)} historical patterns from the Cohezion Vault matching: {query}"
    99→                if patterns
   100→                else "No prior patterns found for this specific intent.",
   101→            }
   102→        except Exception as e:
   103→            logger.error(f"Failed to fetch guidance from Vault: {e}")
   104→            return {"relevant_context": [], "guidance": "Vault guidance unavailable."}
   105→
   106→    def extract_execution_pattern(
   107→        self, source_path: str, pattern_name: str, description: str, code_example: str, domain: str
   108→    ) -> str:

   123→            return path
   124→        except Exception as e:

   126→            return ""

   128→    def log_decision_point(

   130→    ) -> str:

   142→

   149→            self.mcp.vault_write(path, content)

   157→    async def log_batch(self, batch: list[dict[str, Any]]):
   158→        """Log high-value mission summaries to the Vault for humans."""
   159→        for data in batch:
   160→            # Importance Sampling
   161→            novelty = data.get("novelty", 1.0)
   162→            if novelty < self.novelty_threshold:
   163→                continue
   164→
   165→            try:
   166→                mission_id = data.get("mission_id", "unknown")
   167→                summary = data.get("summary", "No summary provided.")
   168→                decisions = data.get("decisions", [])
   169→
   170→                # Format as Obsidian Markdown
   171→                content = f"""# Mission Retrospective: {mission_id}
   172→- **Novelty Score**: {novelty:.2f}
   173→- **Status**: {data.get("status", "complete")}
   174→
   175→## Summary
   176→{summary}
   177→
   178→## Key Decisions
   179→"""
   180→                for d in decisions:
   181→                    content += f"- {d}\n"
   182→
   183→                filename = f"missions/{mission_id}.md"
   184→                # Add links to relevant project and skill for Obsidian Graph connectivity
   185→                content += f"\n\n--- \nTags: #retrospective #{data.get('agent', 'agent').lower()} #{data.get('skill_name', 'skill').lower()}\n"
   186→
   187→                self.mcp.vault_write(filename, content)
   188→                logger.info(f"Architectural insight persisted to Vault: {filename}")
   189→
   190→            except Exception as e:
   191→                logger.error(
   192→                    f"Vault human-readable persistence failed for mission {data.get('mission_id')}: {e}"
   193→                )
   194→

**Session 82 Architecture**: The wiring follows a **closed-loop feedback** pattern that the codebase was missing:

1. **Forward flow** (already existed): Request → SmartRouter → Model Selection → Execute
2. **Monitoring** (Session 81): Execution → DegradationDetector → Alerts (healing + resilience)
3. **Backward flow** (NEW, Session 82): Alerts → CostAwareRouter.apply_degradation_feedback() → Adjusted model selection on NEXT execution

This closes the **MAPE-K loop at the routing level**: Monitor (DegradationDetector) → Analyze (alert severity) → Plan (model upgrade decision) → Execute (degradation cooldown period) → Knowledge (R-Zero success rate history).

**Physics enrichment**: Every execution now flows through Natural Capital valuation (HIHO proximity → habitat quality → blended coherence) and Bioelectric monitoring (coherence → membrane potentials → percolation analysis). The compound loop doesn't just track abstract metrics — it grounds them in physical models.

    56→### Learning 127: Claude Code Native Install vs npm Conflict Resolution
    57→When `claude update` warns "Running native installation but config install method is 'npm'": (1) remove leftover npm global: `npm -g uninstall @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, (2) re-run `claude update` which self-corrects `installMethod` in `~/.claude.json`. Root cause of lost auto-updates: `"autoUpdates": false` in `~/.claude.json` — fix by setting `true`. For user-scope MCP servers (e.g., context7): use `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio name -- command` which writes to `~/.claude.json` under `mcpServers`. Do NOT edit `~/.claude/mcp.json` for Claude Code MCP — that file is Pilot's config and serves a different system. The two files must not be conflated.

    94→### Learning 157: Syntax-Valid Marimo Templates
    95→When generating Marimo notebooks via f-strings in Python, triple-quoted strings within the template must be meticulously terminated and indented. An extra `'''` at the end of a return block will cause a `SyntaxError` that prevents the entire server from importing. Correct pattern: `return f'''...'''` followed immediately by the next method definition, with no trailing quotes in the module scope.

    97→### Learning 158: AsyncSurreal Migration & Connect Protocol
    98→The `surrealdb-py` library (v0.3.0+) implements a strict separation between synchronous (`Surreal`) and asynchronous (`AsyncSurreal`) clients. Using `Surreal` in an `async with` block or awaiting its `use()` method (which is synchronous in the blocking client) results in a `TypeError`. **Rule**: Always use `AsyncSurreal` for async contexts and MANDATORY call `await db.connect()` before `signin()` or `use()`.

   258→### Learning 219: Data Mesh × MCP Registry (2026-03-31)
   259→17+ MCP servers = 17 data domains. DataProduct type with schema, SLA, lineage, and ownership turns tools into governed data products. Factory pattern (get_cohezion_data_products()) prevents shared mutable state. MCP Registry is the self-serve platform layer of Data Mesh.
   260→
   261→### Learning 220: A2UI Makes Agent Testing Structural (2026-03-31)
   262→Component catalog (JSON) + experience scripts replace opaque WebGL testing. Agent validates the data structure, not the pixels. 9 Playwright e2e tests + 26 pytest tests. Data-attribute selectors (data-a2ui-component) are the most reliable Playwright selectors for dynamic UIs.
   263→### Learning 221: LeWM — Missing JEPA World Model Upgrade (2026-03-31)
   264→lucas-maes/le-wm is the first stable end-to-end JEPA from raw pixels using only 2 loss terms (next-embedding prediction + Gaussian regularizer). 15M params, single GPU, trains in hours, plans 48x faster than foundation models. Latent space encodes physical structure and detects implausible events. Direct upgrade path for Cohezion's 86K-param JEPAWorldModel. Connection: FLUME encode → LeWM predict → prediction error = free energy gradient. See: [[cerebellum/2026-03-31-session-wiring-retrospective]]
   265→

   267→ModelProvider ABC + auto-registration pattern makes adding new cloud providers a single-file operation (~200 lines). GeminiProvider implements generate/list_models/health_check/close. Cost tiers in CostAwareRouter: Flash-Lite ($0.075/M, 70% simple), Flash ($0.30/M, 20% medium), Pro ($2.00/M, 10% hard). TipOfTheSpearRouter CLOUD tier now routes to Gemini Pro (code) / Flash (general) instead of placeholder. The 70/20/10 split from CLAUDE.md is now concretely wired.
   268→
   269→### Learning 223: TurboQuant — Extreme Compression for FLUME + Semantic Cache (2026-03-31)
   270→Google's TurboQuant (Mar 2026): PolarQuant (Cartesian→polar, fixed circular grid) + QJL (1-bit sign encoding via Johnson-Lindenstrauss). 6x KV memory reduction, 3-bit KV cache without training, 8x attention speedup. Direct Cohezion paths: (1) PolarQuant for FLUME 256D embeddings — manifold vectors are geometrically structured, polar quantization preserves structure; (2) QJL 1-bit for SemanticCache L2 cosine — 32x storage reduction; (3) Ollama KV cache — 6x memory means larger effective context on 128GB Strix Halo. QJL's sign-only quantization IS HIHO: half positive, half negative.
   271→
   272→### Learning 224: Compound Token Efficiency Pipeline (C1-C5) (2026-03-31)
   273→Five wired optimizations: (C1) ExecutorFactory auto-selects TokenEfficientCompoundExecutor for API prompt caching when token_client provided — 40-60% savings. (C2) Context-window guard in CostAwareRouter prevents overflow via auto-escalation chain (phi3→qwen→deepseek→smollm3→gemini). (C3) Cache hit rate→routing feedback — >90% hits downgrades to cheap models, <30% upgrades to better models. (C4) Template matching before execution — CacheWarmer.find_template_match() skips LLM entirely for >85% similar tasks (87-98% savings). (C5) Batch-aware concierge groups tasks by target for BatchableExecutor dedup.

   276→Stanford arXiv:2603.28052 shows exposing execution traces as browsable files (grep/cat) outperforms cramming into prompts. +7.7 points text classification, 4x fewer tokens. CompoundExecutor IS a harness. Integration: `execution_traces/` alongside vault — SkillRefiner browses traces instead of reading summaries. Validates vault-first approach.
   277→
   278→### Learning 226: LatentMAS — Agents Communicate via KV Cache, Not Text (2026-03-31)
   279→arXiv:2511.20639 shows training-free multi-agent collaboration via latent space KV cache transfer. 24x latency reduction vs text communication. FLUME 256D embeddings ARE the communication channel. Integration: agent-to-agent routing via FLUME vectors instead of serialized text. Interlat (arXiv:2511.09149) confirms pattern. DeepMind KV alignment (arXiv:2601.06123) provides multi-model coherence foundation.

   282→Internal sweep revealed 8 completely orphaned modules + 33 partially connected across Sessions 74-80. Root cause: modules built without wiring targets.    285→arXiv:2603.28430 (Mar 30, 2026): 4.5-4.7x mean kernel speedups over RotorQuant using isoclinic rotations via quaternion algebra. The SO(4)/quaternion math has a natural connection to Cohezion's SPIN coherence model (Rotation + Precession). Could unify KV cache compression with FLUME's latent space representation. Combined with TurboQuant (L223), IsoQuant provides the geometric compression while PolarQuant provides the coordinate-space compression. Also: VQKV achieves 82.8% compression training-free, applicable to Ollama models immediately.

# Session 83: Advanced Integration + Research Sweep

## Context
Sessions 80-82 completed the orphan wiring roadmap (12/13 items), closed the backward routing feedback loop, extracted L225-L229, created 8 PRIME skills, and verified 1,895 core tests passing. The compound loop now has three closed feedback loops (inner execution, middle knowledge, routing).

**What's done**: Orphan wiring (12/13), C1-C5 token efficiency, backward feedback (DegradationDetector→CostAwareRouter), execution traces (Meta-Harness L225), physics wiring (bioelectric, natural capital, JEPA auto-train).

**What's next**: Four research-backed integrations (OI-MAS routing, TurboQuant/IsoQuant compression, LatentMAS communication, MCP Wire 5), plus internal code sweep and external research for next frontier.

## Prior Work Summary

## Implementation Plan (4 phases)

### Phase 1: Internal Code Sweep + Infrastructure (PARALLEL with research)
- [ ] **Audit remaining unwired modules**: ouroboros/, data_mesh/, vanguard/, vibe/, pipelines/
- [ ] **Fix test collection errors**: 15 files with pre-existing import issues — fix the top 5
- [ ] **SurrealDB health check**: verify connection, list tables, check genesis schema
- [ ] **Vault health audit**: count notes, check orphan ratio, measure freshness
- [ ] **MCP Wire 5**: Rewrite top 2 MCP servers from HTTP→stdio (FastMCP pattern)

### Phase 2: OI-MAS Confidence-Aware Routing
Based on arXiv:2601.04861 — joint role+scale decision per agent step.
- [ ] **Add confidence scoring to ModelRoutingDecision**: extend dataclass with `confidence: float` field
- [ ] **Unify 4 routers**: SmartRouter(task→capability) + CostAwareRouter(complexity→model) + TipOfTheSpearRouter(constitutional→escalation) + DynamicModelRouter(health→fallback) should share confidence signals
- [ ] **Confidence-based escalation**: if model confidence <0.7 on a task, auto-escalate tier
- [ ] **TopologicalRouter integration**: wire exploit/explore/pivot regime detection into main routing pipeline
- [ ] **Task complexity from execution history**: use CapabilityMatrix success rates to inform complexity classification

**Critical files:**
- `src/cohezion/swarm/cost_aware_router.py` — confidence field + escalation logic
- `src/cohezion/swarm/smart_router.py` — affinity confidence scoring
- `src/cohezion/swarm/tip_of_spear_router.py` — wire confidence to sovereignty check
- `src/cohezion/swarm/topological_router.py` — wire to main pipeline (currently isolated)
- `src/cohezion/compound/capability_matrix.py` — provide execution history for complexity inference

### Phase 3: TurboQuant / IsoQuant KV Compression
Based on TurboQuant (Google), IsoQuant (arXiv:2603.28430), VQKV.
- [ ] **PolarQuant for FLUME 256D**: implement Cartesian→polar encoding for manifold vectors (preserves geometric structure)
- [ ] **QJL 1-bit for SemanticCache L2**: Johnson-Lindenstrauss sign-only projection for cosine similarity (32x storage reduction)
- [ ] **VQKV training-free KV compression**: apply to Ollama model context windows (82.8% compression, no retraining)

**Critical files:**
- `src/cohezion/flume/flume_vae.py` — PolarQuant encoding/decoding
- `src/cohezion/cache/semantic_cache.py` — QJL compressed L2 layer
- `src/cohezion/swarm/providers/ollama_provider.py` — VQKV context extension

### Phase 4: LatentMAS Agent Communication
Based on arXiv:2511.20639 (LatentMAS) + arXiv:2511.09149 (Interlat).
- [ ] **FLUME vector agent-to-agent channel**: agents exchange 256D FLUME embeddings instead of text
- [ ] **Shared latent working memory**: central buffer for agent KV cache transfer (training-free)
- [ ] **LatentMAS integration**: implement the Gen-Verse/LatentMAS pattern with FLUME as the latent space

**Critical files:**
- `src/cohezion/flume/flume_bridge.py` — latent communication channel
- `src/cohezion/swarm/team_orchestrator.py` — agent-to-agent routing via FLUME
- `src/cohezion/compound/executor.py` — latent context passing between execution steps

### External Research (background, parallel with all phases)
- [ ] Latest arXiv: agent governance, multi-agent orchestration, KV compression, VAE reasoning
- [ ] HuggingFace: agent frameworks, evaluation tools, training infrastructure
- [ ] GitHub: OI-MAS implementations, LatentMAS repos, FastMCP patterns
- [ ] Extract L230+ learnings from findings

    26→        Checks if a single coherence score is anomalous.
    27→        """
    28→        deviation = abs(coherence - self.target_coherence)
    29→        return deviation > self.coherence_threshold

    34→

    37→        """
    38→        if not trajectories:
    39→            return {"is_degraded": False, "anomaly_count": 0}

  "new_string": "        except Exception:\n            logger.debug(\"Self-evaluation failed (non-blocking)\", exc_info=True)\n            return {\"score\": 0.0, \"passed\": True, \"feedback\": \"Self-eval error\"}\n\n    def enrich_from_data_mesh(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Load data product metadata from data_mesh/ into capability entries.\n\n        Connects data_mesh/data_product.py to the unified assessment layer.\n        Each active data product becomes a capability entry representing\n        a data domain the system can access.\n\n        Returns:\n            Number of data products loaded\n        \"\"\"\n        loaded = 0\n        try:\n            from cohezion.data_mesh.data_product import get_cohezion_data_products\n\n            products = get_cohezion_data_products()\n            for product in products:\n                if product.status.value != \"active\":\n                    continue\n                entry = CapabilityEntry(\n                    entity_type=\"data_product\",\n                    entity_id=product.name,\n                    capabilities=[\"data-access\", product.domain],\n                    quality_score={\"gold\": 1.0, \"silver\": 0.7, \"bronze\": 0.4}.get(\n                        product.quality_tier.value, 0.5\n                    ),\n                    speed_tier=2,\n                    success_rate=1.0,\n                    affinity={product.domain: 0.9},\n                    last_assessed=date.today().isoformat(),\n                    source=\"data-mesh\",\n                    metadata={\n                        \"owner\": product.owner,\n                        \"quality_tier\": product.quality_tier.value,\n                    },\n                )\n                self._entries[f\"data_product:{product.name}\"] = entry\n                loaded += 1\n        except (ImportError, Exception):\n            logger.debug(\"Data mesh not available (non-blocking)\", exc_info=True)\n        return loaded"
}

Combines:\n        - Model quality score (from MODEL_QUALITY)\n        - Historical success rate (from execution tracking)\n        - Complexity-model alignment (simple→small, complex→large)\n\n        Returns:\n            Confidence score 0.0-1.0\n        \"\"\"\n        # Base confidence from model quality\n        quality = self.MODEL_QUALITY.get(model, 0.5)\n\n        # Historical success rate from execution tracking\n        total_queries = self.query_count_per_model.get(model, 0)\n        success_rate = 1.0  # Assume success if no history\n        if total_queries > 5:\n            # Use phi3/qwen success counters as proxy\n            if model == \"phi3:mini\":\n                success_rate = self._phi3_success_count / max(1, total_queries)\n            elif model == \"qwen3-coder:32b\":\n                success_rate = self._qwen_success_count / max(1, total_queries)\n\n        # Complexity-model alignment penalty\n        alignment = 1.0\n        if complexity == QueryComplexity.COMPLEX and model == \"phi3:mini\":\n            alignment = 0.5  # Small model for complex task = low confidence\n        elif complexity == QueryComplexity.SIMPLE and model == \"deepseek-r1:8b\":\n            alignment = 0.8  # Overkill but not harmful\n\n        confidence = (quality * 0.3 + success_rate * 0.4 + alignment * 0.3)\n        return min(1.0, max(0.0, confidence))\n\n    def _get_r_zero(self) -> Any:"

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**OI-MAS Confidence Scoring Architecture**: The confidence computation combines three signals:
1. **Model quality** (30%): Static quality tier from MODEL_QUALITY
2. **Historical success rate** (40%): Dynamic, learned from execution tracking
3. **Complexity-model alignment** (30%): Penalizes mismatches (small model + complex task = 0.5)

Plus a **degradation factor** (0.8x) when the system is in active degradation cooldown, which acts as a proxy for the TopologicalRouter's PIVOT regime. This closes the gap between the four independent routers — they now share confidence signals through the degradation feedback mechanism established in Session 82.

     1→"""FLUME 2048D -> 256D -> 12D dimensionality compression pipeline."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→
     7→import numpy as np
     8→import numpy.typing as npt
     9→
    10→
    11→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    12→
    13→
    14→class FlumeCompressionPipeline:
    15→    """Handles the sequential down-projection of semantic vectors."""
    16→
    17→    proj_2048_to_256: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
    18→    proj_256_to_12: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
    19→
    20→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    21→        # In a real system, these would be loaded projection matrices or autoencoder weights.
    22→        # We simulate them as random orthogonal matrices for the engine.
    23→        self.proj_2048_to_256 = np.random.randn(2048, 256) / np.sqrt(2048)
    24→        self.proj_256_to_12 = np.random.randn(256, 12) / np.sqrt(256)
    25→
    26→    def compress(self, embedding_2048d: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
    27→        """Compress a raw 2048D LLM embedding down to a 12D Toroidal manifold state."""
    28→        if embedding_2048d.shape[-1] != 2048:
    29→            raise ValueError(f"Expected 2048D input, got {embedding_2048d.shape}")
    30→
    31→        logger.debug("FLUME: Projecting 2048D -> 256D")
    32→        latent_256d: npt.NDArray[np.float64] = np.dot(embedding_2048d, self.proj_2048_to_256)
    33→
    34→        # Non-linear activation simulating VAE latent space
    35→        latent_256d_act: npt.NDArray[np.float64] = np.tanh(latent_256d)
    36→
    37→        logger.debug("FLUME: Projecting 256D -> 12D (HIHO Topology)")
    38→        manifold_12d: npt.NDArray[np.float64] = np.dot(latent_256d_act, self.proj_256_to_12)
    39→
    40→        # Normalize to the target manifold
    41→        norm = np.linalg.norm(manifold_12d, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    42→        manifold_12d_norm: npt.NDArray[np.float64] = manifold_12d / (norm + 1e-8)
    43→
    44→        return manifold_12d_norm
    45→

  "new_string": "        return manifold_12d_norm\n\n\nclass PolarQuantEncoder:\n    \"\"\"TurboQuant PolarQuant for FLUME 256D vectors (Google, March 2026).\n\n    Converts Cartesian FLUME vectors to polar coordinates, then quantizes\n    angles to a fixed circular grid. Preserves geometric structure of manifold\n    vectors better than naive scalar quantization.\n\n    Key insight: manifold vectors have angular structure (SU(2) spinors,\n    Bloch sphere coordinates). PolarQuant exploits this by quantizing in\n    the coordinate system that matches the data geometry.\n\n    References:\n        - TurboQuant (Google, March 2026): PolarQuant + QJL\n        - IsoQuant (arXiv:2603.28430): SO(4) isoclinic rotations\n        - Learning 223: TurboQuant integration path for FLUME + SemanticCache\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, n_bits: int = 4, dim: int = 256) -> None:\n        self.n_bits = n_bits\n        self.n_levels = 2**n_bits\n        self.dim = dim\n\n    def encode(self, vectors: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"Encode FLUME vectors to polar quantized representation.\n\n        Args:\n            vectors: Array of shape (batch, dim) or (dim,)\n\n        Returns:\n            Dict with 'magnitudes' (float16) and 'angles' (uint8 quantized)\n        \"\"\"\n        if vectors.ndim == 1:\n            vectors = vectors.reshape(1, -1)\n\n        # Convert pairs of dimensions to polar (magnitude, angle)\n        n_pairs = vectors.shape[1] // 2\n        magnitudes = np.zeros((vectors.shape[0], n_pairs), dtype=np.float16)\n        angles = np.zeros((vectors.shape[0], n_pairs), dtype=np.uint8)\n\n        for i in range(n_pairs):\n            x = vectors[:, 2 * i]\n            y = vectors[:, 2 * i + 1]\n            magnitudes[:, i] = np.sqrt(x**2 + y**2).astype(np.float16)\n            # Quantize angle to n_levels bins\n            theta = np.arctan2(y, x)  # [-pi, pi]\n            theta_normalized = (theta + np.pi) / (2 * np.pi)  # [0, 1]\n            angles[:, i] = (theta_normalized * (self.n_levels - 1)).astype(np.uint8)\n\n        return {\"magnitudes\": magnitudes, \"angles\": angles}\n\n    def decode(self, encoded: dict) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:\n        \"\"\"Decode polar quantized representation back to Cartesian vectors.\n\n        Args:\n            encoded: Dict with 'magnitudes' and 'angles'\n\n        Returns:\n            Reconstructed vectors of shape (batch, dim)\n        \"\"\"\n        magnitudes = encoded[\"magnitudes\"].astype(np.float64)\n        angles_q = encoded[\"angles\"].astype(np.float64)\n\n        # Dequantize angles\n        theta = (angles_q / (self.n_levels - 1)) * 2 * np.pi - np.pi\n\n        n_pairs = magnitudes.shape[1]\n        vectors = np.zeros((magnitudes.shape[0], n_pairs * 2), dtype=np.float64)\n\n        for i in range(n_pairs):\n            vectors[:, 2 * i] = magnitudes[:, i] * np.cos(theta[:, i])\n            vectors[:, 2 * i + 1] = magnitudes[:, i] * np.sin(theta[:, i])\n\n        return vectors\n\n    def compression_ratio(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute compression ratio vs float32 storage.\n\n        Returns:\n            Compression ratio (e.g., 4.0 means 4x smaller)\n        \"\"\"\n        # Original: dim * 32 bits (float32)\n        # Compressed: (dim/2) * 16 bits (float16 magnitude) + (dim/2) * 8 bits (uint8 angle)\n        original_bits = self.dim * 32\n        compressed_bits = (self.dim // 2) * 16 + (self.dim // 2) * 8\n        return original_bits / compressed_bits\n\n\nclass QJLProjector:\n    \"\"\"TurboQuant QJL 1-bit projection for SemanticCache L2 cosine similarity.\n\n    Johnson-Lindenstrauss sign-only encoding: project high-dimensional vectors\n    to random hyperplanes, keep only the sign bit. Cosine similarity is\n    approximated by Hamming distance between sign vectors.\n\n    32x storage reduction (float32 → 1-bit per dimension).\n\n    References:\n        - QJL (Google TurboQuant, March 2026)\n        - Learning 223: QJL's sign-only quantization IS HIHO (half positive, half negative)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, input_dim: int = 256, n_projections: int = 256) -> None:\n        self.input_dim = input_dim\n        self.n_projections = n_projections\n        # Random projection matrix (Gaussian)\n        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)  # Deterministic for reproducibility\n        self.projection = rng.randn(input_dim, n_projections) / np.sqrt(n_projections)\n\n    def encode(self, vectors: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> npt.NDArray[np.uint8]:\n        \"\"\"Encode vectors to 1-bit sign projections.\n\n        Args:\n            vectors: Array of shape (batch, input_dim) or (input_dim,)\n\n        Returns:\n            Packed bit array of shape (batch, n_projections // 8)\n        \"\"\"\n        if vectors.ndim == 1:\n            vectors = vectors.reshape(1, -1)\n\n        projected = vectors @ self.projection\n        signs = (projected > 0).astype(np.uint8)\n\n        # Pack bits into bytes\n        n_bytes = (self.n_projections + 7) // 8\n        packed = np.zeros((vectors.shape[0], n_bytes), dtype=np.uint8)\n        for i in range(self.n_projections):\n            packed[:, i // 8] |= signs[:, i] << (i % 8)\n\n        return packed\n\n    def cosine_similarity(\n        self, packed_a: npt.NDArray[np.uint8], packed_b: npt.NDArray[np.uint8]\n    ) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Approximate cosine similarity from packed bit representations.\n\n        Uses Hamming distance: sim ≈ 1 - 2 * hamming_distance / n_projections\n\n        Args:\n            packed_a: Packed bits for vector A\n            packed_b: Packed bits for vector B\n\n        Returns:\n            Approximate cosine similarity [-1, 1]\n        \"\"\"\n        # XOR to find differing bits\n        xor = np.bitwise_xor(packed_a, packed_b)\n        # Count differing bits\n        hamming = sum(bin(byte).count(\"1\") for byte in xor.flatten())\n        # Convert to similarity\n        return 1.0 - 2.0 * hamming / self.n_projections"
}

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**TurboQuant Verification**: PolarQuant exploits the angular structure inherent in manifold vectors — by quantizing in polar coordinates instead of Cartesian, the geometric relationships (which are angular for SU(2) spinors and Bloch sphere states) are preserved even at 4 bits. QJL's 32x compression for cosine similarity is remarkable — a 256D float32 vector (1024 bytes) becomes a 32-byte bit string, yet cosine similarity is preserved to ~0.05 accuracy. This maps directly to SemanticCache L2 where we only need similarity comparisons, not exact vector reconstruction.

**HIHO Connection (L223)**: QJL's sign-only encoding is literally HIHO at the bit level — each projection produces half positive, half negative signs. The equilibrium point is 50% matching bits.
