  "content": "\"\"\"MXFP4 GEMM via load_inline Custom HIP Kernel.\n\nStrategy: Bypass Python API ceiling by compiling HIP C++ at runtime.\nUses torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline() which is proven on Popcorn runner.\n\nApproach: MFMA-tiled GEMM with fused FP4 unpacking and E8M0 scaling.\nTarget: <10us from current 22.8us baseline.\n\nReferences:\n- K-Search (arXiv:2602.19128) for systematic optimization\n- HipKittens (arXiv:2511.08083) for tile primitives\n- CK-Tile gfx950 MXFP4 support\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport torch\nfrom torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline\n\nfrom task import input_t, output_t\n\n# HIP C++ source for MXFP4 GEMM kernel\nHIP_SOURCE = r\"\"\"\n#include <torch/extension.h>\n#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>\n#include <hip/hip_bf16.h>\n\n// MXFP4 unpacking: 2 values per uint8 byte\n__device__ __forceinline__ float unpack_fp4_lo(uint8_t byte) {\n    // Low nibble: MXFP4 values [0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6]\n    static __device__ const float LUT[16] = {\n        0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 1.5f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 6.0f,\n        -0.0f, -0.5f, -1.0f, -1.5f, -2.0f, -3.0f, -4.0f, -6.0f\n    };\n    return LUT[byte & 0xF];\n}\n\n__device__ __forceinline__ float unpack_fp4_hi(uint8_t byte) {\n    static __device__ const float LUT[16] = {\n        0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 1.5f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 6.0f,\n        -0.0f, -0.5f, -1.0f, -1.5f, -2.0f, -3.0f, -4.0f, -6.0f\n    };\n    return LUT[(byte >> 4) & 0xF];\n}\n\n// E8M0 scale: f32 = 2^(e8m0 - 127)\n__device__ __forceinline__ float e8m0_to_float(uint8_t val) {\n    return exp2f((float)((int)val - 127));\n}\n\n// Simple MXFP4 GEMM kernel: C = A @ B^T with FP4 inputs and E8M0 scales\n// Each thread computes one output element (naive, will be tiled later)\n__global__ void mxfp4_gemm_naive(\n    const uint8_t* __restrict__ A_packed,   // [M, K/2] packed FP4\n    const uint8_t* __restrict__ B_packed,   // [N, K/2] packed FP4\n    const uint8_t* __restrict__ A_scale,    // [M, K/32] E8M0 scales\n    const uint8_t* __restrict__ B_scale,    // [N, K/32] E8M0 scales\n    at::BFloat16* __restrict__ C,           // [M, N] output\n    int M, int N, int K\n) {\n    int row = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    int col = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n\n    if (row >= M || col >= N) return;\n\n    float acc = 0.0f;\n    int K_half = K / 2;\n    int scale_stride_a = K / 32;\n    int scale_stride_b = K / 32;\n\n    for (int k = 0; k < K_half; k++) {\n        // Unpack two FP4 values from each byte\n        uint8_t a_byte = A_packed[row * K_half + k];\n        uint8_t b_byte = B_packed[col * K_half + k];\n\n        float a_lo = unpack_fp4_lo(a_byte);\n        float a_hi = unpack_fp4_hi(a_byte);\n        float b_lo = unpack_fp4_lo(b_byte);\n        float b_hi = unpack_fp4_hi(b_byte);\n\n        // Apply E8M0 scales (one scale per 32 elements)\n        int scale_idx = (2 * k) / 32;\n        float sa = e8m0_to_float(A_scale[row * scale_stride_a + scale_idx]);\n        float sb = e8m0_to_float(B_scale[col * scale_stride_b + scale_idx]);\n\n        acc += a_lo * b_lo * sa * sb;\n        acc += a_hi * b_hi * sa * sb;\n    }\n\n    C[row * N + col] = __float2bfloat16(acc);\n}\n\n// Python-callable wrapper\ntorch::Tensor mxfp4_gemm_hip(\n    torch::Tensor A_packed,\n    torch::Tensor B_packed,\n    torch::Tensor A_scale,\n    torch::Tensor B_scale,\n    int M, int N, int K\n) {\n    auto C = torch::empty({M, N}, torch::TensorOptions()\n        .dtype(torch::kBFloat16)\n        .device(A_packed.device()));\n\n    dim3 block(16, 16);\n    dim3 grid((N + block.x - 1) / block.x, (M + block.y - 1) / block.y);\n\n    mxfp4_gemm_naive<<<grid, block, 0, at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()>>>(\n        A_packed.data_ptr<uint8_t>(),\n        B_packed.data_ptr<uint8_t>(),\n        A_scale.data_ptr<uint8_t>(),\n        B_scale.data_ptr<uint8_t>(),\n        reinterpret_cast<at::BFloat16*>(C.data_ptr()),\n        M, N, K\n    );\n\n    return C;\n}\n\nPYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME, m) {\n    m.def(\"mxfp4_gemm_hip\", &mxfp4_gemm_hip, \"MXFP4 GEMM via HIP\");\n}\n\"\"\"\n\nCPP_SOURCE = \"torch::Tensor mxfp4_gemm_hip(torch::Tensor, torch::Tensor, torch::Tensor, torch::Tensor, int, int, int);\"\n\n# Compile at import time\ntry:\n    _module = load_inline(\n        name=\"mxfp4_gemm_hip\",\n        cpp_sources=[CPP_SOURCE],\n        cuda_sources=[HIP_SOURCE],\n        functions=[\"mxfp4_gemm_hip\"],\n        verbose=False,\n        extra_cuda_cflags=[\"-O3\", \"--offload-arch=gfx950\"],\n    )\n    HAS_CUSTOM_KERNEL = True\nexcept Exception as e:\n    print(f\"load_inline failed: {e}, falling back to reference\")\n    HAS_CUSTOM_KERNEL = False\n\n\ndef custom_kernel(input: input_t) -> output_t:\n    \"\"\"Run custom HIP MXFP4 GEMM kernel.\"\"\"\n    A, B, A_scale, B_scale = input.A, input.B, input.A_scale, input.B_scale\n    M, K_half = A.shape\n    N = B.shape[0]\n    K = K_half * 2\n\n    return _module.mxfp4_gemm_hip(A, B, A_scale, B_scale, M, N, K)\n\n\ndef ref_kernel(input: input_t) -> output_t:\n    \"\"\"Reference kernel (baseline anchor).\"\"\"\n    from aiter import gemm_a4w4\n    return gemm_a4w4(input.A, input.B, input.A_scale, input.B_scale)\n\n\ndef kernel(input: input_t) -> output_t:\n    \"\"\"Two Builders: try custom, fall back to reference.\"\"\"\n    if HAS_CUSTOM_KERNEL:\n        return custom_kernel(input)\n    return ref_kernel(input)\n"

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**This is a v1 naive kernel** — it computes one output element per thread without MFMA instructions or shared memory tiling. It will be slower than the API baseline, but it proves the `load_inline` compilation path works on the runner. The optimization path is clear: (1) add shared memory tiling with BLOCK_M/N/K, (2) use MFMA instructions for matrix multiply, (3) add 8-wave ping-pong scheduling from HipKittens, (4) fuse quantization. Each step is a K-Search mutation that the compound kernel cycle can benchmark.

**The Two Builders pattern is embedded**: `kernel()` tries custom first, falls back to `ref_kernel()` (aiter baseline) if compilation fails. The correctness anchor is always available.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

    11→
    12→The only path to beating the API ceiling is fusing quant into the GEMM kernel,
    13→which requires custom HIP compilation (blocked by runner source scanning).

    16→import aiter
    17→from aiter import dtypes
    18→from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant
    19→from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import e8m0_shuffle
    20→from task import input_t, output_t

    23→def _choose_log2_k_split(m: int, n: int, k: int) -> int:
    24→    """Optimal log2_k_split for MI355X (gfx950) from skill data."""
    25→    if m <= 32:
    26→        return 3  # High split for low occupancy
    27→    if m <= 128:
    28→        return 2
    29→    if m <= 512:
    30→        return 1

    34→def custom_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
    35→    A, B, B_q, B_shuffle, B_scale_sh = data
    36→    m, k = A.shape
    37→    n = B.shape[0]
    38→
    39→    # Quantize A to MXFP4 with shuffled E8M0 scales

    42→    A_scale_sh = e8m0_shuffle(A_scale_e8m0).view(dtypes.fp8_e8m0)
    43→    A_q = A_q.view(dtypes.fp4x2)

     1→"""
     2→FP4 quant + FP4 GEMM reference: bf16 A, MXFP4 B -> MXFP4 per-1x32 quant A -> gemm_a4w4 -> bf16 C.
     3→Quant logic follows aiter op_tests/test_gemm_a4w4.py (get_triton_quant(QuantType.per_1x32)).
     4→
     5→NOTE: Explicitly uses dynamic_mxfp4_quant from aiter.ops.triton.quant (patched in #975)
     6→      rather than going through aiter.get_triton_quant, which may dispatch to the
     7→      unpatched fp4_utils.py kernel. See ROCm/aiter#974, ROCm/aiter#975.
     8→"""
     9→
    10→import aiter
    11→import torch
    12→from aiter import dtypes
    13→from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_weight
    14→from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant  # #975-patched kernel
    15→from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import e8m0_shuffle
    16→from task import input_t, output_t
    17→from utils import make_match_reference
    18→
    19→
    20→# K must be divisible by 64 (scale group 32 and fp4 pack 2)
    21→SCALE_GROUP_SIZE = 32
    22→
    23→
    24→def _quant_mxfp4(x, shuffle=True):
    25→    x_fp4, bs_e8m0 = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(x)
    26→    if shuffle:
    27→        bs_e8m0 = e8m0_shuffle(bs_e8m0)
    28→    return x_fp4.view(dtypes.fp4x2), bs_e8m0.view(dtypes.fp8_e8m0)
    29→
    30→
    31→def generate_input(m: int, n: int, k: int, seed: int):  # -> input_t:
    32→    """
    33→    Generate random bf16 inputs A [m, k], B [n, k] and quantized MXFP4 B, shuffled B and B_scale.
    34→
    35→    Returns:
    36→        Tuple of (A, B), both bf16 on cuda.
    37→    """
    38→    assert k % 64 == 0, "k must be divisible by 64 (scale group 32 and fp4 pack 2)"
    39→    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda")
    40→    gen.manual_seed(seed)
    41→    A = torch.randn((m, k), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", generator=gen)
    42→    B = torch.randn((n, k), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", generator=gen)
    43→    B_q, B_scale_sh = _quant_mxfp4(B, shuffle=True)
    44→    # shuffle B(weight) to (16,16) tile coalesced
    45→    B_shuffle = shuffle_weight(B_q, layout=(16, 16))
    46→    return (A, B, B_q, B_shuffle, B_scale_sh)
    47→
    48→
    49→def run_torch_fp4_mm(
    50→    x: torch.Tensor,
    51→    w: torch.Tensor,
    52→    x_scales: torch.Tensor,
    53→    w_scales: torch.Tensor,
    54→    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
    55→) -> torch.Tensor:
    56→    """
    57→    PyTorch reference: dequant MXFP4 + E8M0 scale -> f32 -> mm -> dtype.
    58→    Same logic as aiter op_tests/test_gemm_a4w4.run_torch.
    59→    x: [m, k//2] fp4 packed, w: [n, k//2] fp4 packed
    60→    x_scales: [m, k//32] E8M0, w_scales: [n, k//32] E8M0
    61→    Returns: [m, n] in dtype
    62→    """
    63→    from aiter.utility import fp4_utils
    64→
    65→    m, _ = x.shape
    66→    n, _ = w.shape
    67→    # fp4 packed -> f32
    68→    x_f32 = fp4_utils.mxfp4_to_f32(x)
    69→    w_f32 = fp4_utils.mxfp4_to_f32(w)
    70→    # E8M0 scale: [*, k//32] -> repeat 32 along k -> f32
    71→    x_scales = x_scales[:m].repeat_interleave(SCALE_GROUP_SIZE, dim=1)
    72→    x_scales_f32 = fp4_utils.e8m0_to_f32(x_scales)
    73→    x_f32 = x_f32 * x_scales_f32
    74→    w_scales = w_scales[:n].repeat_interleave(SCALE_GROUP_SIZE, dim=1)
    75→    w_scales_f32 = fp4_utils.e8m0_to_f32(w_scales)
    76→    w_f32 = w_f32 * w_scales_f32
    77→    return torch.mm(x_f32, w_f32.T).to(dtype)[:m, :n]
    78→
    79→
    80→def ref_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
    81→    """
    82→    Reference: MXFP4 per-1x32 quant on A and B; both PyTorch ref and gemm_a4w4 are given.
    83→    Returns gemm_a4w4 for check_implementation.
    84→    """
    85→    A, B, B_q, B_shuffle, B_scale_sh = data
    86→    A = A.contiguous()
    87→    B = B.contiguous()
    88→    m, k = A.shape
    89→    n, _ = B.shape
    90→
    91→    # 1) PyTorch impl just for your reference: dequant fp4 + e8m0 -> f32 -> mm -> bf16
    92→    # Per-1x32 MXFP4 quant
    93→    # A_q, A_scale = _quant_mxfp4(A, shuffle=False)
    94→    # B_q, B_scale = _quant_mxfp4(B, shuffle=False)
    95→
    96→    # gemm_a4w4 expects A [M,K/2], B [N,K/2] as dtypes.fp4x2; A_scale/B_scale [*,K/32] E8M0
    97→    # quant_func returns scale as dtypes.fp8_e8m0; gemm_a4w4 accepts E8M0, no view to uint8 needed
    98→    # slice to exact shapes [m,k_scale] / [n,k_scale] (quant may return padded scale)
    99→
   100→    # k_scale = k // SCALE_GROUP_SIZE
   101→    # A_scale = A_scale[:m, :k_scale].contiguous()
   102→    # B_scale = B_scale[:n, :k_scale].contiguous()
   103→    # out_torch = run_torch_fp4_mm(A_q, B_q, A_scale, B_scale, torch.bfloat16)
   104→
   105→    # 2) aiter.gemm_a4w4 path: needs shuffled B_q and shuffled scales (see test_gemm_a4w4.py:102-105)
   106→    A_q, A_scale_sh = _quant_mxfp4(A, shuffle=True)
   107→    # to be noted, aiter also has other a4w4 implements using triton, https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/main/aiter/ops/triton/gemm/basic/gemm_afp4wfp4.py
   108→    out_gemm = aiter.gemm_a4w4(
   109→        A_q,
   110→        B_shuffle,
   111→        A_scale_sh,
   112→        B_scale_sh,
   113→        dtype=dtypes.bf16,
   114→        bpreshuffle=True,
   115→    )
   116→    return out_gemm
   117→
   118→
   119→check_implementation = make_match_reference(ref_kernel, rtol=1e-02, atol=1e-02)
   120→

     1→"""MXFP4 GEMM Breakthrough: Stream-Aware Custom HIP Kernel.
     2→
     3→Target: 4.3µs (leader) vs current ~13.4µs
     4→Strategy: Custom HIP kernel with explicit stream synchronization to bypass 'work on another stream' error.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→import ctypes
     8→import os
     9→import subprocess
    10→import sys
    11→import tempfile
    12→from pathlib import Path
    13→
    14→import torch
    15→import aiter
    16→from aiter import dtypes
    17→from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant
    18→from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import e8m0_shuffle
    19→from task import input_t, output_t
    20→
    21→# ─── HIP Kernel Source (Stream-Aware) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    22→HIP_SOURCE = r'''
    23→#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
    24→#include <hip/hip_bf16.h>
    25→#include <stdint.h>
    26→
    27→#define WARP_SIZE 64
    28→#define BLOCK_M 128
    29→#define BLOCK_N 128
    30→#define BLOCK_K 128
    31→
    32→__device__ __forceinline__ float unpack_fp4(uint8_t val) {
    33→    float sign = ((val >> 3) & 0x1) ? -1.0f : 1.0f;
    34→    float exp = (val >> 2) & 0x1;
    35→    float mant = val & 0x3;
    36→    return exp ? sign * (1.0f + mant * 0.5f) : sign * mant * 0.125f;
    37→}
    38→
    39→__device__ __forceinline__ float e8m0_to_float(uint8_t val) {
    40→    int exp = (int)val - 127;
    41→    return exp2f((float)exp);
    42→}
    43→
    44→__global__ void mxfp4_gemm_kernel(
    45→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ A_fp4,
    46→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ B_fp4,
    47→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ A_scale,
    48→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ B_scale,
    49→    __hip_bfloat16* __restrict__ C,
    50→    int M, int N, int K
    51→) {
    52→    int m_block = blockIdx.y * BLOCK_M;
    53→    int n_block = blockIdx.x * BLOCK_N;
    54→    int tid = threadIdx.x;
    55→    
    56→    int local_m = tid / BLOCK_N;
    57→    int local_n = tid % BLOCK_N;
    58→    
    59→    float acc = 0.0f;
    60→    
    61→    for (int k = 0; k < K; k += 32) {
    62→        int k_group = k / 32;
    63→        
    64→        for (int k_off = 0; k_off < 32 && (k + k_off) < K; k_off++) {
    65→            int global_k = k + k_off;
    66→            
    67→            int a_idx = (m_block + local_m) * (K / 2) + (global_k / 2);
    68→            uint8_t a_packed = A_fp4[a_idx];
    69→            uint8_t a_val = (global_k % 2 == 0) ? (a_packed & 0xF) : (a_packed >> 4);
    70→            
    71→            int b_idx = (n_block + local_n) * (K / 2) + (global_k / 2);
    72→            uint8_t b_packed = B_fp4[b_idx];
    73→            uint8_t b_val = (global_k % 2 == 0) ? (b_packed & 0xF) : (b_packed >> 4);
    74→            
    75→            float a_scale = e8m0_to_float(A_scale[(m_block + local_m) * (K / 32) + k_group]);
    76→            float b_scale = e8m0_to_float(B_scale[(n_block + local_n) * (K / 32) + k_group]);
    77→            
    78→            acc += unpack_fp4(a_val) * a_scale * unpack_fp4(b_val) * b_scale;
    79→        }
    80→    }
    81→    
    82→    int c_idx = (m_block + local_m) * N + (n_block + local_n);
    83→    if ((m_block + local_m) < M && (n_block + local_n) < N) {
    84→        C[c_idx] = __float2bfloat16(acc);
    85→    }
    86→}
    87→
    88→extern "C" int launch_mxfp4_gemm(
    89→    void* A_fp4, void* B_fp4,
    90→    void* A_scale, void* B_scale,
    91→    void* C, int M, int N, int K,
    92→    hipStream_t stream
    93→) {
    94→    dim3 grid((N + BLOCK_N - 1) / BLOCK_N, (M + BLOCK_M - 1) / BLOCK_M);
    95→    dim3 block(BLOCK_M * BLOCK_N);
    96→    
    97→    hipLaunchKernelGGL(mxfp4_gemm_kernel, grid, block, 0, stream,
    98→        (const uint8_t*)A_fp4, (const uint8_t*)B_fp4,
    99→        (const uint8_t*)A_scale, (const uint8_t*)B_scale,
   100→        (__hip_bfloat16*)C, M, N, K);
   101→    
   102→    return hipGetLastError();
   103→}
   104→'''
   105→
   106→# ─── JIT Compilation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   107→_lib = None
   108→
   109→def _compile():
   110→    global _lib
   111→    if _lib is not None: return _lib
   112→    
   113→    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
   114→        src = Path(tmpdir) / "kernel.hip"
   115→        src.write_text(HIP_SOURCE)
   116→        so = Path(tmpdir) / "libkernel.so"
   117→        
   118→        # MI355X (gfx950) flags
   119→        cmd = [
   120→            "/opt/rocm/bin/hipcc", "-O3", "-fPIC", "--offload-arch=gfx950",
   121→            "-shared", "-o", str(so), str(src)
   122→        ]
   123→        res = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
   124→        if res.returncode != 0:
   125→            print(f"Compilation failed: {res.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
   126→            return None
   127→            
   128→        lib = ctypes.CDLL(str(so))
   129→        lib.launch_mxfp4_gemm.argtypes = [
   130→            ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p,
   131→            ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int,
   132→            ctypes.c_void_p
   133→        ]
   134→        _lib = lib
   135→        return lib
   136→
   137→def custom_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
   138→    A, B, B_q, B_shuffle, B_scale_sh = data
   139→    M, K = A.shape
   140→    N = B.shape[0]
   141→
   142→    # Standard AITER Quantization
   143→    A_q, A_scale_e8m0 = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(A.contiguous())
   144→    A_scale_sh = e8m0_shuffle(A_scale_e8m0).view(dtypes.fp8_e8m0)
   145→    A_q = A_q.view(dtypes.fp4x2)
   146→
   147→    # Attempt custom HIP with stream synchronization
   148→    lib = _compile()
   149→    if lib:
   150→        C = torch.empty((M, N), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
   151→        # EXPLICIT STREAM PASSING
   152→        stream = ctypes.c_void_p(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
   153→        
   154→        err = lib.launch_mxfp4_gemm(
   155→            ctypes.c_void_p(A_q.data_ptr()),
   156→            ctypes.c_void_p(B_shuffle.data_ptr()),
   157→            ctypes.c_void_p(A_scale_sh.data_ptr()),
   158→            ctypes.c_void_p(B_scale_sh.data_ptr()),
   159→            ctypes.c_void_p(C.data_ptr()),
   160→            M, N, K,
   161→            stream
   162→        )
   163→        if err == 0: return C
   164→
   165→    # Fallback to standard AITER
   166→    return aiter.gemm_a4w4(
   167→        A_q, B_shuffle, A_scale_sh, B_scale_sh,
   168→        dtype=dtypes.bf16, bpreshuffle=True,
   169→    )
   170→

     1→// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
     2→// HipKittens Fused MoE Kernel for MI355X (gfx950)
     3→// Optimized for <110µs latency target (Rank 1: 109.8µs)
     4→//
     5→// Key Optimizations:
     6→// - 2-stage fused pipeline (Gate+Up → SiLU → Down)
     7→// - Register-resident intermediate activations
     8→// - MXFP4 dequantization with E8M0 scales
     9→// - Explicit MFMA instruction usage
    10→
    11→#pragma once
    12→
    13→#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
    14→#include <hip/hip_bf16.h>
    15→#include <hip/hip_fp8.h>
    16→
    17→// HipKittens header
    18→#include <hipkittens/kittens.cuh>
    19→
    20→namespace hk = kittens;
    21→
    22→// Type aliases
    23→using bf16 = __hip_bfloat16;
    24→using bf16_2 = __hip_bfloat162;
    25→using fp8e4m3 = __hip_fp8_e4m3;
    26→using fp8e4m3_4 = __hip_fp8x4_e4m3;
    27→
    28→// ==============================================================================
    29→// Device Helper Functions
    30→// ==============================================================================
    31→
    32→__device__ __forceinline__ float silu(float x) {
    33→    return x / (1.0f + expf(-x));
    34→}
    35→
    36→__device__ __forceinline__ bf16_2 silu_bf16_2(bf16_2 x) {
    37→    float2 f = make_float2(__bfloat162float(x.x), __bfloat162float(x.y));
    38→    f.x = silu(f.x);
    39→    f.y = silu(f.y);
    40→    return make_bfloat162(f.x, f.y);
    41→}
    42→
    43→// MXFP4 dequantization
    44→// 4-bit float format with shared exponent (E8M0 scale)
    45→__device__ __forceinline__ float mxfp4_to_float(uint8_t val4, float scale) {
    46→    // MXFP4: S E1 E0 M (sign, 2-bit exponent, 1-bit mantissa)
    47→    bool sign = (val4 >> 3) & 1;
    48→    int exp = (val4 >> 1) & 0x3;
    49→    int mant = val4 & 1;
    50→
    51→    // Value table:
    52→    // exp=0: 0
    53→    // exp=1: 0.5 + mant*0.5 = 0.5 or 1.0
    54→    // exp=2: 1.0 + mant*0.5 = 1.0 or 1.5
    55→    // exp=3: 2.0 * (1 + mant) = 2.0 or 4.0
    56→    float val = 0.0f;
    57→    if (exp == 1) val = mant ? 1.0f : 0.5f;
    58→    else if (exp == 2) val = mant ? 1.5f : 1.0f;
    59→    else if (exp == 3) val = mant ? 4.0f : 2.0f;
    60→
    61→    return sign ? -val * scale : val * scale;
    62→}
    63→
    64→// Dequantize 8 packed MXFP4 values (32 bits = 8 x 4 bits)
    65→__device__ __forceinline__ void dequantize_mxfp4x8(
    66→    uint32_t packed,
    67→    float scale,
    68→    float* out
    69→) {
    70→    #pragma unroll
    71→    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
    72→        uint8_t val4 = (packed >> (i * 4)) & 0xF;
    73→        out[i] = mxfp4_to_float(val4, scale);
    74→    }
    75→}
    76→
    77→// ==============================================================================
    78→// 2-Stage Fused MoE Kernel
    79→// ==============================================================================
    80→//
    81→// This kernel fuses both GEMM stages into a single launch:
    82→// Stage 1: hidden @ gate_up_w.T -> SiLU + Mul
    83→// Stage 2: activated @ down_w.T -> output
    84→//
    85→// Template parameters tuned for DeepSeek-R1 on MI355X
    86→// - HIDDEN_SIZE = 7168
    87→// - INTERMEDIATE_SIZE = 256 (per expert)
    88→// - BLOCK_M = 64 (tokens per block)
    89→// - BLOCK_N = 128 (dims per block)
    90→// - BLOCK_K = 64 (K dimension tiles)
    91→
    92→template<int HIDDEN_SIZE, int INTERMEDIATE_SIZE, int BLOCK_M=64, int BLOCK_N=128, int BLOCK_K=64>
    93→__global__ __launch_bounds__(256, 2)
    94→void fused_moe_hipkittens_kernel(
    95→    const bf16* __restrict__ hidden_states,     // [num_tokens, HIDDEN_SIZE]
    96→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ gate_up_weights,  // [num_experts, 2*INTERMEDIATE_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE/2] MXFP4
    97→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ down_weights,     // [num_experts, HIDDEN_SIZE, INTERMEDIATE_SIZE/2] MXFP4
    98→    const float* __restrict__ gate_up_scales,   // [num_experts, 2*INTERMEDIATE_SIZE] E8M0
    99→    const float* __restrict__ down_scales,      // [num_experts, HIDDEN_SIZE] E8M0
   100→    const int32_t* __restrict__ sorted_token_ids,
   101→    const int32_t* __restrict__ sorted_expert_ids,
   102→    const float* __restrict__ sorted_weights,
   103→    bf16* __restrict__ output,
   104→    int num_tokens,
   105→    int num_experts,
   106→    int topk,
   107→    int num_tiles
   108→) {
   109→    // Block info
   110→    int tile_idx = blockIdx.x;
   111→    if (tile_idx >= num_tiles) return;
   112→
   113→    int expert_id = sorted_expert_ids[tile_idx];
   114→    int token_base = tile_idx * BLOCK_M;
   115→
   116→    // Thread info
   117→    int warp_id = threadIdx.x / 64;   // 4 warps per block (256 threads)
   118→    int lane_id = threadIdx.x % 64;
   119→    int warp_m = warp_id / 2;          // 2x2 warp arrangement
   120→    int warp_n = warp_id % 2;
   121→
   122→    // Shared memory layout
   123→    // Double-buffered for input tiles
   124→    __shared__ bf16 smem_hidden[2][BLOCK_M * BLOCK_K];  // Input activation
   125→    __shared__ float smem_gate_up[INTERMEDIATE_SIZE * 2]; // Stage 1 output
   126→    __shared__ float smem_activated[INTERMEDIATE_SIZE];   // After SiLU*Up
   127→
   128→    // Register accumulators for Stage 1
   129→    // Each warp computes partial results
   130→    constexpr int WARP_M = BLOCK_M / 2;  // 32 tokens per warp
   131→    constexpr int WARP_N = BLOCK_N / 2; // 64 dims per warp
   132→
   133→    float acc_gate[WARP_N] = {0.0f};
   134→    float acc_up[WARP_N] = {0.0f};
   135→
   136→    // ===== STAGE 1: Gate + Up Projection =====
   137→    // Iterate over HIDDEN_SIZE in BLOCK_K tiles
   138→
   139→    #pragma unroll 2
   140→    for (int k_base = 0; k_base < HIDDEN_SIZE; k_base += BLOCK_K) {
   141→        // Load hidden states to shared memory (coalesced access)
   142→        // Each thread loads multiple elements
   143→        int load_elems = (BLOCK_M * BLOCK_K) / 256;
   144→        int smem_buffer = (k_base / BLOCK_K) & 1;  // Double buffer toggle
   145→
   146→        #pragma unroll
   147→        for (int i = 0; i < load_elems; i++) {
   148→            int idx = threadIdx.x * load_elems + i;
   149→            int sm_row = idx / BLOCK_K;
   150→            int sm_col = idx % BLOCK_K;
   151→            int global_token = token_base + sm_row;
   152→            int global_col = k_base + sm_col;
   153→
   154→            if (global_token < num_tokens * topk && global_col < HIDDEN_SIZE) {
   155→                int token_idx = sorted_token_ids[global_token];
   156→                smem_hidden[smem_buffer][sm_row * BLOCK_K + sm_col] =
   157→                    hidden_states[token_idx * HIDDEN_SIZE + global_col];
   158→            } else {
   159→                smem_hidden[smem_buffer][sm_row * BLOCK_K + sm_col] = bf16(0);
   160→            }
   161→        }
   162→
   163→        __syncthreads();
   164→
   165→        // Compute partial products using MFMA-style accumulation
   166→        // Each warp handles a sub-tile
   167→        int warp_row_offset = warp_m * WARP_M;
   168→        int warp_col_offset = warp_n * WARP_N;
   169→
   170→        // Weight base pointer for this expert
   171→        const uint8_t* gate_w_base = gate_up_weights + expert_id * (2 * INTERMEDIATE_SIZE) * (HIDDEN_SIZE / 2);
   172→        const uint8_t* up_w_base = gate_w_base + INTERMEDIATE_SIZE * (HIDDEN_SIZE / 2);
   173→        const float* gate_s_base = gate_up_scales + expert_id * 2 * INTERMEDIATE_SIZE;
   174→        const float* up_s_base = gate_s_base + INTERMEDIATE_SIZE;
   175→
   176→        // Compute partial products for this K tile
   177→        #pragma unroll
   178→        for (int n = 0; n < WARP_N; n++) {
   179→            int global_n = warp_col_offset + n;
   180→            if (global_n >= INTERMEDIATE_SIZE) continue;
   181→
   182→            float scale_gate = gate_s_base[global_n];
   183→            float scale_up = up_s_base[global_n];
   184→
   185→            // Accumulate across K dimension
   186→            #pragma unroll
   187→            for (int k = lane_id; k < BLOCK_K; k += 64) {
   188→                int global_k = k_base + k;
   189→                if (global_k >= HIDDEN_SIZE) continue;
   190→
   191→                // Load activation
   192→                int smem_idx = warp_row_offset * BLOCK_K + k;
   193→                float act_val = __bfloat162float(smem_hidden[smem_buffer][smem_idx]);
   194→
   195→                // Load and dequantize weights (packed 4-bit)
   196→                // Each weight element is 4 bits, so 2 per byte
   197→                int w_idx = global_n * (HIDDEN_SIZE / 2) + global_k / 2;
   198→                int byte_idx = w_idx / 2;  // 2 4-bit values per byte
   199→                int nibble_idx = w_idx & 1; // High or low nibble
   200→
   201→                uint8_t packed_gate = (gate_w_base[byte_idx] >> (nibble_idx * 4)) & 0xF;
   202→                uint8_t packed_up = (up_w_base[byte_idx] >> (nibble_idx * 4)) & 0xF;
   203→
   204→                float w_gate = mxfp4_to_float(packed_gate, scale_gate);
   205→                float w_up = mxfp4_to_float(packed_up, scale_up);
   206→
   207→                // FMA
   208→                acc_gate[n] = fmaf(act_val, w_gate, acc_gate[n]);
   209→                acc_up[n] = fmaf(act_val, w_up, acc_up[n]);
   210→            }
   211→        }
   212→
   213→        __syncthreads();
   214→    }
   215→
   216→    // Warp reduction for parallel lanes
   217→    #pragma unroll
   218→    for (int n = 0; n < WARP_N; n++) {
   219→        // Reduce across warp using warp shuffle
   220→        #pragma unroll
   221→        for (int offset = 32; offset > 0; offset /= 2) {
   222→            acc_gate[n] += __shfl_down(acc_gate[n], offset);
   223→            acc_up[n] += __shfl_down(acc_up[n], offset);
   224→        }
   225→    }
   226→
   227→    // Store Stage 1 results to shared memory
   228→    if (lane_id == 0) {
   229→        #pragma unroll
   230→        for (int n = 0; n < WARP_N; n++) {
   231→            int global_n = warp_n * WARP_N + n;
   232→            if (global_n < INTERMEDIATE_SIZE) {
   233→                smem_gate_up[warp_m * INTERMEDIATE_SIZE + global_n] = acc_gate[n];
   234→                smem_gate_up[(1 + warp_m) * INTERMEDIATE_SIZE + global_n] = acc_up[n];
   235→            }
   236→        }
   237→    }
   238→
   239→    __syncthreads();
   240→
   241→    // ===== SiLU + Mul Fusion =====
   242→    // Each thread handles part of intermediate dimension
   243→    #pragma unroll
   244→    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < INTERMEDIATE_SIZE; i += 256) {
   245→        float gate_val = smem_gate_up[i];
   246→        float up_val = smem_gate_up[INTERMEDIATE_SIZE + i];
   247→        smem_activated[i] = silu(gate_val) * up_val;
   248→    }
   249→
   250→    __syncthreads();
   251→
   252→    // ===== STAGE 2: Down Projection =====
   253→    float acc_out[WARP_N] = {0.0f};
   254→
   255→    const uint8_t* down_w_base = down_weights + expert_id * HIDDEN_SIZE * (INTERMEDIATE_SIZE / 2);
   256→    const float* down_s_base = down_scales + expert_id * HIDDEN_SIZE;
   257→
   258→    // Iterate over HIDDEN_SIZE output dimension
   259→    #pragma unroll 2
   260→    for (int n2_base = 0; n2_base < HIDDEN_SIZE; n2_base += BLOCK_N) {
   261→        int warp_col_out = n2_base + warp_n * WARP_N;
   262→
   263→        // Load activated values for this output tile
   264→        // Reuse smem_gate_up for activated values
   265→        __syncthreads();  // Ensure activated is ready
   266→
   267→        // Compute down projection
   268→        #pragma unroll
   269→        for (int n2 = 0; n2 < WARP_N; n2++) {
   270→            int global_n2 = warp_col_out + n2;
   271→            if (global_n2 >= HIDDEN_SIZE) continue;
   272→
   273→            float scale_down = down_s_base[global_n2];
   274→
   275→            // Accumulate over INTERMEDIATE_SIZE
   276→            #pragma unroll
   277→            for (int k2 = 0; k2 < INTERMEDIATE_SIZE; k2 += 8) {
   278→                // Load 8 activated values
   279→                float act_vals[8];
   280→                #pragma unroll
   281→                for (int kk = 0; kk < 8 && (k2 + kk) < INTERMEDIATE_SIZE; kk++) {
   282→                    act_vals[kk] = smem_activated[k2 + kk];
   283→                }
   284→
   285→                // Load and dequantize down weights
   286→                int w_idx = global_n2 * (INTERMEDIATE_SIZE / 2) + k2 / 2;
   287→                int byte_idx = w_idx / 2;
   288→
   289→                #pragma unroll
   290→                for (int kk = 0; kk < 8 && (k2 + kk) < INTERMEDIATE_SIZE; kk += 2) {
   291→                    uint8_t packed_down = down_w_base[byte_idx + kk/2];
   292→                    uint8_t w_low = packed_down & 0xF;
   293→                    uint8_t w_high = (packed_down >> 4) & 0xF;
   294→
   295→                    acc_out[n2] = fmaf(act_vals[kk], mxfp4_to_float(w_low, scale_down), acc_out[n2]);
   296→                    if (kk + 1 < INTERMEDIATE_SIZE - k2) {
   297→                        acc_out[n2] = fmaf(act_vals[kk+1], mxfp4_to_float(w_high, scale_down), acc_out[n2]);
   298→                    }
   299→                }
   300→            }
   301→        }
   302→
   303→        __syncthreads();
   304→    }
   305→
   306→    // ===== Write Output with Top-K Weighting =====
   307→    #pragma unroll
   308→    for (int n2 = 0; n2 < WARP_N; n2++) {
   309→        int global_n = warp_n * WARP_N + n2;
   310→        if (global_n >= HIDDEN_SIZE) continue;
   311→
   312→        #pragma unroll
   313→        for (int m = 0; m < WARP_M; m++) {
   314→            int global_token = token_base + warp_m * WARP_M + m;
   315→            if (global_token >= num_tokens * topk) continue;
   316→
   317→            int token_idx = sorted_token_ids[global_token];
   318→            float weight = sorted_weights[global_token];
   319→            float final_val = acc_out[n2] * weight;
   320→
   321→            // Atomic add for multi-expert accumulation
   322→            int out_idx = token_idx * HIDDEN_SIZE + global_n;
   323→            #if __gfx950__
   324→            atomicAdd((float*)&output[out_idx], final_val);
   325→            #else
   326→            // Use uint32_t atomic for compatibility
   327→            union { float f; uint32_t u; } val;
   328→            val.f = final_val;
   329→            uint32_t old_val = atomicAdd((uint32_t*)&output[out_idx], val.u);
   330→            // Note: This is approximate atomic add for BF16
   331→            #endif
   332→        }
   333→    }
   334→}
   335→

   337→// Host Launch Functions
   338→// ==============================================================================
   339→
   340→template<int HIDDEN_SIZE, int INTERMEDIATE_SIZE>
   341→struct FusedMoeKernelLauncher {
   342→    static void launch(
   343→        const bf16* hidden_states,
   344→        const uint8_t* gate_up_weights,
   345→        const uint8_t* down_weights,
   346→        const float* gate_up_scales,
   347→        const float* down_scales,
   348→        const int32_t* sorted_token_ids,
   349→        const int32_t* sorted_expert_ids,
   350→        const float* sorted_weights,

   353→        int num_experts,
   354→        int topk,

   357→    ) {

   360→        constexpr int BLOCK_K = 64;

   364→
   365→        fused_moe_hipkittens_kernel<HIDDEN_SIZE, INTERMEDIATE_SIZE, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K>

   370→            output, num_tokens, num_experts, topk, num_tiles

   372→    }

Now I have enough context. Let me build the GEMM v2 tiled kernel. The key insight is that the v1 naive kernel has each thread compute one output element — that's terrible for GPU utilization. V2 needs shared memory tiling with cooperative thread loading.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**GEMM Tiling for AMD MI355X (gfx950):**
1. The naive kernel (v1) is memory-bound: each thread independently reads A and B from global memory, causing massive redundant loads. Shared memory tiling lets a thread block cooperatively load tiles of A and B, then each thread reuses the shared data across multiple K iterations.
2. MI355X has 304 CUs with 8 XCDs (Accelerated Compute Dies). Optimal tile sizes need to fill all XCDs — BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128 gives 1 tile per ~16K output elements, which maps well to the CU count for typical GEMM shapes.
3. The MXFP4 format packs 2 values per byte with E8M0 scales (one scale per 32 elements). Tiling along K in chunks of 32 aligns perfectly with the scale group boundary.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

     1→"""MXFP4 GEMM via load_inline Custom HIP Kernel.
     2→
     3→Strategy: Bypass Python API ceiling by compiling HIP C++ at runtime.
     4→Uses torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline() which is proven on Popcorn runner.
     5→
     6→Approach: MFMA-tiled GEMM with fused FP4 unpacking and E8M0 scaling.
     7→Target: <10us from current 22.8us baseline.
     8→
     9→References:
    10→- K-Search (arXiv:2602.19128) for systematic optimization
    11→- HipKittens (arXiv:2511.08083) for tile primitives
    12→- CK-Tile gfx950 MXFP4 support
    13→"""
    14→
    15→import os
    16→import torch
    17→from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline
    18→
    19→from task import input_t, output_t
    20→
    21→# HIP C++ source for MXFP4 GEMM kernel
    22→HIP_SOURCE = r"""
    23→#include <torch/extension.h>
    24→#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
    25→#include <hip/hip_bf16.h>
    26→
    27→// MXFP4 unpacking: 2 values per uint8 byte
    28→__device__ __forceinline__ float unpack_fp4_lo(uint8_t byte) {
    29→    // Low nibble: MXFP4 values [0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6]
    30→    static __device__ const float LUT[16] = {
    31→        0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 1.5f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 6.0f,
    32→        -0.0f, -0.5f, -1.0f, -1.5f, -2.0f, -3.0f, -4.0f, -6.0f
    33→    };
    34→    return LUT[byte & 0xF];
    35→}
    36→
    37→__device__ __forceinline__ float unpack_fp4_hi(uint8_t byte) {
    38→    static __device__ const float LUT[16] = {
    39→        0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 1.5f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 6.0f,
    40→        -0.0f, -0.5f, -1.0f, -1.5f, -2.0f, -3.0f, -4.0f, -6.0f
    41→    };
    42→    return LUT[(byte >> 4) & 0xF];
    43→}
    44→
    45→// E8M0 scale: f32 = 2^(e8m0 - 127)
    46→__device__ __forceinline__ float e8m0_to_float(uint8_t val) {
    47→    return exp2f((float)((int)val - 127));
    48→}
    49→
    50→// Simple MXFP4 GEMM kernel: C = A @ B^T with FP4 inputs and E8M0 scales
    51→// Each thread computes one output element (naive, will be tiled later)
    52→__global__ void mxfp4_gemm_naive(
    53→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ A_packed,   // [M, K/2] packed FP4
    54→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ B_packed,   // [N, K/2] packed FP4
    55→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ A_scale,    // [M, K/32] E8M0 scales
    56→    const uint8_t* __restrict__ B_scale,    // [N, K/32] E8M0 scales
    57→    at::BFloat16* __restrict__ C,           // [M, N] output
    58→    int M, int N, int K
    59→) {
    60→    int row = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
    61→    int col = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    62→
    63→    if (row >= M || col >= N) return;
    64→
    65→    float acc = 0.0f;
    66→    int K_half = K / 2;
    67→    int scale_stride_a = K / 32;
    68→    int scale_stride_b = K / 32;
    69→
    70→    for (int k = 0; k < K_half; k++) {
    71→        // Unpack two FP4 values from each byte
    72→        uint8_t a_byte = A_packed[row * K_half + k];
    73→        uint8_t b_byte = B_packed[col * K_half + k];
    74→
    75→        float a_lo = unpack_fp4_lo(a_byte);
    76→        float a_hi = unpack_fp4_hi(a_byte);
    77→        float b_lo = unpack_fp4_lo(b_byte);
    78→        float b_hi = unpack_fp4_hi(b_byte);
    79→
    80→        // Apply E8M0 scales (one scale per 32 elements)
    81→        int scale_idx = (2 * k) / 32;
    82→        float sa = e8m0_to_float(A_scale[row * scale_stride_a + scale_idx]);
    83→        float sb = e8m0_to_float(B_scale[col * scale_stride_b + scale_idx]);
    84→
    85→        acc += a_lo * b_lo * sa * sb;
    86→        acc += a_hi * b_hi * sa * sb;
    87→    }
    88→
    89→    C[row * N + col] = __float2bfloat16(acc);
    90→}
    91→
    92→// Python-callable wrapper
    93→torch::Tensor mxfp4_gemm_hip(
    94→    torch::Tensor A_packed,
    95→    torch::Tensor B_packed,
    96→    torch::Tensor A_scale,
    97→    torch::Tensor B_scale,

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**V2 Tiling Architecture:**
1. **Scale-aligned K tiles**: Each K tile is exactly 32 FP4 elements (16 bytes) = 1 E8M0 scale group. This means each scale value is loaded once and applied to all 32 elements — no redundant scale lookups.
2. **Thread-to-output mapping**: 256 threads in a 16×16 grid, each computing a 4×4 sub-tile = 64×64 output. The compute-to-load ratio is much better than naive (4× arithmetic per load).
3. **Constant memory LUT**: The FP4 decode table is in `__constant__` memory (broadcast to all threads in one cycle) vs v1's `static __device__` (per-thread L1 cache pressure).
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Generate Cohezion status report — kernel optimization + system health.\n\nQueries SurrealDB for kernel runs, training history, health checks.\nOptionally emails via SMTP (requires COHEZION_SMTP_* env vars).\nAlways writes to --output file.\n\nUsage:\n    .venv/bin/python scripts/generate_status_report.py --output report.txt\n    .venv/bin/python scripts/generate_status_report.py --email manderson240@gmail.com\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport os\nimport smtplib\nimport sys\nimport urllib.request\nfrom base64 import b64encode\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom email.mime.text import MIMEText\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSURREAL_URL = \"http://localhost:8001/sql\"\nSURREAL_HEADERS = {\n    \"Accept\": \"application/json\",\n    \"surreal-ns\": \"cohezion\",\n    \"surreal-db\": \"cohezion\",\n    \"Authorization\": \"Basic \" + b64encode(b\"root:root\").decode(),\n}\n\nKERNEL_LEADERS = {\"gemm\": 4.3, \"mla\": 33.0, \"moe\": 109.8}\n\n\ndef surreal_query(sql: str) -> list:\n    try:\n        req = urllib.request.Request(\n            SURREAL_URL, data=sql.encode(), headers=SURREAL_HEADERS, method=\"POST\"\n        )\n        resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)\n        return json.loads(resp.read())\n    except Exception:\n        return []\n\n\ndef get_kernel_summary() -> str:\n    lines = [\"=== Kernel Optimization Status ===\\n\"]\n    for kernel, leader in KERNEL_LEADERS.items():\n        results = surreal_query(\n            f\"SELECT math::min(time_us) as best, count() as total \"\n            f\"FROM kernel_run WHERE kernel = '{kernel}' GROUP ALL;\"\n        )\n        best = 999999.0\n        total = 0\n        if results and results[0].get(\"status\") == \"OK\" and results[0].get(\"result\"):\n            row = results[0][\"result\"][0]\n            best = row.get(\"best\", 999999.0) or 999999.0\n            total = row.get(\"total\", 0) or 0\n\n        gap = best / leader if leader > 0 else 0\n        lines.append(f\"  {kernel.upper():5s}  best={best:8.1f}us  leader={leader:.1f}us  gap={gap:.1f}x  runs={total}\")\n\n        # Recent runs (last hour)\n        recent = surreal_query(\n            f\"SELECT approach, time_us, status, created FROM kernel_run \"\n            f\"WHERE kernel = '{kernel}' AND created > time::now() - 1h ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 5;\"\n        )\n        if recent and recent[0].get(\"status\") == \"OK\" and recent[0].get(\"result\"):\n            for r in recent[0][\"result\"]:\n                lines.append(\n                    f\"    {r.get('approach', '?')[:30]:30s} {r.get('time_us', 0):8.1f}us [{r.get('status', '?')}]\"\n                )\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef get_system_health() -> str:\n    lines = [\"\\n=== System Health ===\\n\"]\n\n    # SurrealDB table counts\n    for table in [\"kernel_run\", \"training_run\", \"learning\", \"health_check\", \"retrospection\"]:\n        results = surreal_query(f\"SELECT count() as n FROM {table} GROUP ALL;\")\n        n = 0\n        if results and results[0].get(\"status\") == \"OK\" and results[0].get(\"result\"):\n            n = results[0][\"result\"][0].get(\"n\", 0) or 0\n        lines.append(f\"  SurrealDB {table}: {n} records\")\n\n    # Test suite status\n    try:\n        import subprocess\n\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [\"uv\", \"run\", \"pytest\", \"tests/\", \"-q\", \"--tb=no\", \"-o\", \"addopts=\"],\n            capture_output=True,\n            text=True,\n            timeout=120,\n            cwd=str(Path(__file__).parent.parent),\n        )\n        # Parse \"X passed, Y warnings\" from last line\n        for line in result.stdout.strip().split(\"\\n\")[-3:]:\n            if \"passed\" in line or \"failed\" in line:\n                lines.append(f\"  Tests: {line.strip()}\")\n                break\n    except Exception as e:\n        lines.append(f\"  Tests: could not run ({e})\")\n\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef get_recent_learnings() -> str:\n    lines = [\"\\n=== Recent Learnings (last 2h) ===\\n\"]\n    results = surreal_query(\n        \"SELECT content, category, created FROM learning \"\n        \"WHERE created > time::now() - 2h ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 5;\"\n    )\n    if results and results[0].get(\"status\") == \"OK\" and results[0].get(\"result\"):\n        for r in results[0][\"result\"]:\n            content = (r.get(\"content\") or \"\")[:80]\n            cat = r.get(\"category\", \"?\")\n            lines.append(f\"  [{cat}] {content}\")\n    else:\n        lines.append(\"  No new learnings in last 2 hours\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef generate_report() -> str:\n    now = datetime.now().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\")\n    deadline = \"April 6, 2026 11:59 PM PST\"\n\n    header = f\"\"\"Cohezion Status Report — {now}\nDeadline: {deadline}\n{'=' * 60}\n\"\"\"\n    kernel_summary = get_kernel_summary()\n    health = get_system_health()\n    learnings = get_recent_learnings()\n\n    footer = f\"\"\"\n{'=' * 60}\nGenerated by scripts/generate_status_report.py\nNext report in ~1 hour\n\"\"\"\n    return header + kernel_summary + health + learnings + footer\n\n\ndef send_email(report: str, recipient: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Send email via SMTP. Requires env vars for SMTP config.\"\"\"\n    smtp_host = os.environ.get(\"COHEZION_SMTP_HOST\", \"\")\n    smtp_port = int(os.environ.get(\"COHEZION_SMTP_PORT\", \"587\"))\n    smtp_user = os.environ.get(\"COHEZION_SMTP_USER\", \"\")\n    smtp_pass = os.environ.get(\"COHEZION_SMTP_PASS\", \"\")\n\n    if not smtp_host or not smtp_user:\n        print(\"SMTP not configured (set COHEZION_SMTP_HOST, COHEZION_SMTP_USER, COHEZION_SMTP_PASS)\")\n        return False\n\n    msg = MIMEText(report)\n    msg[\"Subject\"] = f\"Cohezion Kernel Status — {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}\"\n    msg[\"From\"] = smtp_user\n    msg[\"To\"] = recipient\n\n    try:\n        with smtplib.SMTP(smtp_host, smtp_port) as server:\n            server.starttls()\n            server.login(smtp_user, smtp_pass)\n            server.send_message(msg)\n        print(f\"Email sent to {recipient}\")\n        return True\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"Email failed: {e}\")\n        return False\n\n\ndef is_substantial(report: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Check if report has substantial content worth sending.\"\"\"\n    # Always send if there are new kernel runs in last hour\n    if \"success\" in report.lower() and \"runs=\" in report:\n        return True\n    # Always send if there are new learnings\n    if \"No new learnings\" not in report:\n        return True\n    # Send anyway as heartbeat (but could be made conditional)\n    return True\n\n\ndef main():\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Generate Cohezion status report\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--output\", help=\"Output file path\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--email\", help=\"Email recipient\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--force\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"Send even if not substantial\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n\n    report = generate_report()\n\n    # Write to file\n    if args.output:\n        Path(args.output).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        Path(args.output).write_text(report)\n        print(f\"Report written to {args.output}\")\n\n    # Print to stdout\n    print(report)\n\n    # Email if configured and substantial\n    if args.email:\n        if args.force or is_substantial(report):\n            send_email(report, args.email)\n        else:\n            print(\"No substantial updates — skipping email\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

    34→# Aggressive thresholds — wider matmul regime
    35→MATMUL_MAX_BS = 16  # was 8
    36→MATMUL_MAX_TOTAL_KV = 131072  # was 65536
    37→A16W8_THRESHOLD = 524288  # expanded
    38→
    39→_cache: dict = {}
    40→_scratch: dict = {}
    41→
    42→
    43→def _get_scratch(name, shape, dtype):
    44→    key = (name, shape, dtype)
    45→    if key not in _scratch:
    46→        _scratch[key] = torch.empty(shape, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
    47→    return _scratch[key]
    48→
    49→
    50→def _get_meta(bs, qsl, kvsl, qdt, kvdt, qo_ind, kv_ind, splits):
    51→    key = (bs, qsl, kvsl, qdt, kvdt, splits)
    52→    if key in _cache:
    53→        return _cache[key]
    54→
    55→    nq, nkv = NUM_HEADS, NUM_KV_HEADS
    56→    kv_last = (kv_ind[1:] - kv_ind[:-1]).to(torch.int32)
    57→    info = get_mla_metadata_info_v1(
    58→        bs, qsl, nq, qdt, kvdt,
    59→        is_sparse=False, fast_mode=True,  # enabled fast_mode
    60→        num_kv_splits=splits, intra_batch_mode=True,
    61→    )
    62→    work = [torch.empty(s, dtype=t, device="cuda") for s, t in info]
    63→    wm, wi, wis, ri, rfm, rpm = work
    64→    get_mla_metadata_v1(
    65→        qo_ind, kv_ind, kv_last, nq // nkv, nkv, True,
    66→        wm, wis, wi, ri, rfm, rpm,
    67→        page_size=PAGE_SIZE, kv_granularity=max(PAGE_SIZE, 16),
    68→        max_seqlen_qo=qsl, uni_seqlen_qo=qsl,
    69→        fast_mode=True, max_split_per_batch=splits,
    70→        intra_batch_mode=True, dtype_q=qdt, dtype_kv=kvdt,
    71→    )
    72→    tq = bs * qsl
    73→    tkv = int(kv_ind[-1].item())
    74→    meta = {
    75→        "wm": wm, "wi": wi, "wis": wis, "ri": ri, "rfm": rfm, "rpm": rpm,
    76→        "kvi": torch.arange(tkv, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    77→        "kvl": kv_last,
    78→        "logits": torch.empty((splits, tq, nq, V_HEAD_DIM), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda"),
    79→        "lse": torch.empty((splits, tq, nq), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda"),
    80→        "out": torch.empty((tq, nq, V_HEAD_DIM), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"),
    81→    }
    82→    _cache[key] = meta
    83→    return meta
    84→
    85→
    86→def custom_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
    87→    q, kv_data, qo_indptr, kv_indptr, config = data
    88→    bs = config["batch_size"]
    89→    qsl = config["q_seq_len"]
    90→    kvsl = config["kv_seq_len"]
    91→    total_kv = bs * kvsl
    92→
    93→    # ── Regime 1: matmul (aggressive boundary) ──
    94→    if bs <= MATMUL_MAX_BS or total_kv <= MATMUL_MAX_TOTAL_KV:
    95→        kv = kv_data["bf16"]
    96→        # Reshape directly without view() if possible
    97→        q3 = q.reshape(bs, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM)
    98→        kv_b = kv.reshape(bs, kvsl, QK_HEAD_DIM)
    99→        
   100→        # Q@K^T with in-place scale and fused softmax path
   101→        # Using bfloat16 for intermediate scores to exploit loose tolerance
   102→        scores = torch.bmm(q3, kv_b.transpose(1, 2))
   103→        scores.mul_(SM_SCALE)
   104→        
   105→        # In-place softmax in bf16
   106→        weights = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
   107→        
   108→        v_b = kv_b[:, :, :V_HEAD_DIM]
   109→        out = torch.bmm(weights, v_b)
   110→        return out.reshape(bs * qsl, NUM_HEADS, V_HEAD_DIM)
   111→
   112→    # ── Regime 2+3: ASM dispatch ──
   113→    kv_fp8, kv_scale = kv_data["fp8"]
   114→    
   115→    # Fast quantization with scratch buffer
   116→    finfo = torch.finfo(FP8_DTYPE)
   117→    q_abs = q.abs()
   118→    amax = q_abs.amax().clamp_(min=1e-12)
   119→    q_scale = amax.div_(finfo.max)
   120→    q_fp8 = q.div(q_scale).clamp_(min=finfo.min, max=finfo.max).to(FP8_DTYPE)
   121→    q_scale_f32 = q_scale.to(torch.float32).reshape(1)
   122→
   123→    splits = _choose_splits(total_kv)
   124→    kv_4d = kv_fp8.reshape(kv_fp8.shape[0], PAGE_SIZE, NUM_KV_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM)
   125→
   126→    m = _get_meta(bs, qsl, kvsl, q_fp8.dtype, kv_fp8.dtype, qo_indptr, kv_indptr, splits)
   127→
   128→    mla_decode_stage1_asm_fwd(
   129→        q_fp8.reshape(-1, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM), kv_4d,
   130→        qo_indptr, kv_indptr, m["kvi"], m["kvl"],
   131→        None, m["wm"], m["wi"], m["wis"],
   132→        qsl, PAGE_SIZE, NUM_KV_HEADS, SM_SCALE,
   133→        m["logits"], m["lse"], m["out"], q_scale_f32, kv_scale,
   134→    )
   135→    mla_reduce_v1(
   136→        m["logits"], m["lse"], m["ri"], m["rfm"], m["rpm"],
   137→        qsl, m["out"], None,
   138→    )
   139→    return m["out"]

     1→"""
     2→Reference implementation for MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) decode kernel.
     3→
     4→Uses aiter MLA kernels (mla_decode_fwd) as the reference.
     5→DeepSeek R1 forward_absorb MLA: absorbed q (576), compressed kv_buffer (576),
     6→output v_head_dim = kv_lora_rank = 512.

     8→The input provides:
     9→  q:       (total_q, 16, 576) bfloat16 — absorbed query
    10→  kv_data: dict with KV cache in three formats:
    11→    "bf16":  Tensor  (total_kv, 1, 576)  bfloat16          — highest precision
    12→    "fp8":   (Tensor, Tensor)  kv_buffer fp8 + scalar scale — per-tensor quantized
    13→    "mxfp4": (Tensor, Tensor)  kv_buffer fp4x2 + fp8_e8m0  — block-32 quantized
    14→  The reference quantizes Q to fp8 on-the-fly inside ref_kernel.
    15→
    16→The reference kernel quantizes Q to fp8 on-the-fly and uses fp8 KV (a8w8 kernel),
    17→which is ~2-3x faster than bf16 on MI355X with negligible accuracy loss.
    18→
    19→Decode only — persistent mode with get_mla_metadata_v1.
    20→"""
    21→
    22→import torch
    23→from aiter import dtypes as aiter_dtypes
    24→from aiter import get_mla_metadata_info_v1, get_mla_metadata_v1
    25→from aiter.mla import mla_decode_fwd
    26→from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import (
    27→    dynamic_mxfp4_quant,
    28→    e8m0_to_f32,
    29→    mxfp4_to_f32,
    30→)
    31→from task import input_t, output_t
    32→from utils import make_match_reference
    33→
    34→
    35→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    36→# DeepSeek R1 latent MQA constants (forward_absorb path)
    37→# https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528/blob/main/config.json
    38→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    39→NUM_HEADS = 16
    40→NUM_KV_HEADS = 1
    41→KV_LORA_RANK = 512
    42→QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM = 64
    43→QK_HEAD_DIM = KV_LORA_RANK + QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM  # 576
    44→V_HEAD_DIM = KV_LORA_RANK  # 512
    45→SM_SCALE = 1.0 / (QK_HEAD_DIM**0.5)
    46→
    47→PAGE_SIZE = 1
    48→NUM_KV_SPLITS = 32
    49→
    50→# FP8 dtype (platform-specific via aiter)
    51→FP8_DTYPE = aiter_dtypes.fp8
    52→
    53→# Query dtype for the reference kernel: "fp8" or "bf16"
    54→Q_DTYPE = "fp8"
    55→
    56→# KV cache dtype for the reference kernel: "fp8" or "bf16"
    57→KV_DTYPE = "fp8"
    58→
    59→
    60→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    61→# FP8 quantization (sglang style: dynamic per-tensor)
    62→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    63→
    64→
    65→def quantize_fp8(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    66→    """
    67→    Dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization (following sglang scaled_fp8_quant).
    68→
    69→    Args:
    70→        tensor: bf16 tensor to quantize
    71→
    72→    Returns:
    73→        (fp8_tensor, scale) where scale is a scalar float32 tensor.
    74→        Dequantize: fp8_tensor.to(bf16) * scale
    75→    """
    76→    finfo = torch.finfo(FP8_DTYPE)
    77→    amax = tensor.abs().amax().clamp(min=1e-12)
    78→    scale = amax / finfo.max
    79→    fp8_tensor = (tensor / scale).clamp(min=finfo.min, max=finfo.max).to(FP8_DTYPE)
    80→    return fp8_tensor, scale.to(torch.float32).reshape(1)
    81→
    82→
    83→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    84→# MXFP4 quantization (aiter native: block-32, fp4x2 + fp8_e8m0 dtypes)
    85→# Uses aiter.utility.fp4_utils.dynamic_mxfp4_quant
    86→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    87→
    88→
    89→def quantize_mxfp4(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    90→    """
    91→    MXFP4 block-wise quantization using aiter's dynamic_mxfp4_quant.
    92→
    93→    Block size = 32. Each block gets an E8M0 scale factor.
    94→    Two FP4 E2M1 values are packed per byte.
    95→
    96→    Args:
    97→        tensor: bf16 tensor of shape [B, M, N] (N must be divisible by 32)
    98→
    99→    Returns:
   100→        (fp4_data, scale_e8m0)
   101→        - fp4_data:   shape [B, M, N//2] in aiter_dtypes.fp4x2
   102→        - scale_e8m0: shape [B*M, ceil(N/32)] padded, in aiter_dtypes.fp8_e8m0
   103→    """
   104→    orig_shape = tensor.shape  # (B, M, N)
   105→    B, M, N = orig_shape
   106→
   107→    # dynamic_mxfp4_quant expects 2D: (B*M, N)
   108→    tensor_2d = tensor.reshape(B * M, N)
   109→    fp4_data_2d, scale_e8m0 = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(tensor_2d)
   110→
   111→    # Reshape fp4_data back to 3D: (B, M, N//2)
   112→    fp4_data = fp4_data_2d.view(B, M, N // 2)
   113→
   114→    return fp4_data, scale_e8m0
   115→
   116→
   117→def dequantize_mxfp4(
   118→    fp4_data: torch.Tensor,
   119→    scale_e8m0: torch.Tensor,
   120→    orig_shape: tuple,
   121→    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
   122→) -> torch.Tensor:
   123→    """
   124→    Dequantize MXFP4 tensor using aiter utilities.
   125→
   126→    Note: dynamic_mxfp4_quant may pad both row and block dimensions in scale_e8m0.
   127→    We trim scales to match the actual data dimensions.
   128→
   129→    Args:
   130→        fp4_data:   packed FP4 data, shape [B, M, N//2] in fp4x2 or uint8
   131→        scale_e8m0: E8M0 block scale factors (possibly padded) in fp8_e8m0
   132→        orig_shape: original (B, M, N) for reshaping
   133→        dtype:      output dtype
   134→
   135→    Returns:
   136→        Dequantized tensor of shape orig_shape.
   137→    """
   138→    B, M, N = orig_shape
   139→    num_rows = B * M
   140→    block_size = 32
   141→    num_blocks = N // block_size  # actual blocks needed (e.g. 576/32 = 18)
   142→
   143→    # Unpack FP4 to float32: mxfp4_to_f32 expects (..., N//2) -> (..., N)
   144→    fp4_data_2d = fp4_data.reshape(num_rows, N // 2)
   145→    float_vals = mxfp4_to_f32(fp4_data_2d)  # (num_rows, N)
   146→
   147→    # Convert E8M0 scales to float32 and trim padded dimensions
   148→    scale_f32 = e8m0_to_f32(scale_e8m0)  # (padded_rows, padded_blocks)
   149→    scale_f32 = scale_f32[:num_rows, :num_blocks]  # (num_rows, num_blocks)
   150→
   151→    # Apply block scales
   152→    float_vals_blocked = float_vals.view(num_rows, num_blocks, block_size)
   153→    scaled = float_vals_blocked * scale_f32.unsqueeze(-1)
   154→
   155→    return scaled.view(B, M, N).to(dtype)

   315→
   316→def generate_input(batchsize: int, qseqlen: int, kvseqlen: int, seed: int) -> input_t:
   317→    """
   318→    Generate absorbed q and compressed kv_buffer for MLA decode.
   319→
   320→    Returns all three KV cache formats in kv_data dict:
   321→      kv_data = {
   322→        "bf16":  Tensor               — (total_kv, 1, 576) bfloat16
   323→        "fp8":   (Tensor, Tensor)     — kv_buffer fp8 + scalar scale
   324→        "mxfp4": (Tensor, Tensor)     — kv_buffer fp4x2 + fp8_e8m0 scale
   325→      }
   326→    """
   327→    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda")
   328→    gen.manual_seed(seed)
   329→
   330→    total_q = batchsize * qseqlen
   331→    total_kv = batchsize * kvseqlen
   332→
   333→    # Absorbed query: (total_q, num_heads, 576) bf16
   334→    q = torch.randn(
   335→        (total_q, NUM_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM),
   336→        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
   337→        device="cuda",
   338→        generator=gen,
   339→    )
   340→
   341→    # Compressed KV buffer: (total_kv, 1, 576) bf16 — the source of truth
   342→    kv_buffer_bf16 = torch.randn(
   343→        (total_kv, NUM_KV_HEADS, QK_HEAD_DIM),
   344→        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
   345→        device="cuda",
   346→        generator=gen,
   347→    )

   351→
   352→    # Quantize KV to mxfp4
   353→    kv_buffer_mxfp4, kv_scale_mxfp4 = quantize_mxfp4(kv_buffer_bf16)
   354→
   355→    # All three KV formats: bf16 is a Tensor, fp8/mxfp4 are (Tensor, Tensor) tuples
   356→    kv_data = {
   357→        "bf16": kv_buffer_bf16,
   358→        "fp8": (kv_buffer_fp8, kv_scale_fp8),
   359→        "mxfp4": (kv_buffer_mxfp4, kv_scale_mxfp4),
   360→    }
   361→
   362→    qo_indptr = torch.arange(0, batchsize + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") * qseqlen
   363→    kv_indptr = torch.arange(0, batchsize + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") * kvseqlen
   364→
   365→    config = {
   366→        "batch_size": batchsize,
   367→        "num_heads": NUM_HEADS,
   368→        "num_kv_heads": NUM_KV_HEADS,
   369→        "qk_head_dim": QK_HEAD_DIM,
   370→        "kv_lora_rank": KV_LORA_RANK,
   371→        "qk_rope_head_dim": QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM,
   372→        "v_head_dim": V_HEAD_DIM,
   373→        "q_seq_len": qseqlen,
   374→        "kv_seq_len": kvseqlen,
   375→        "sm_scale": SM_SCALE,
   376→    }
   377→
   378→    return (q, kv_data, qo_indptr, kv_indptr, config)

   381→def ref_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
   382→    """Reference MLA decode attention. Uses Q_DTYPE and KV_DTYPE to select kernel variant."""
   383→    q, kv_data, qo_indptr, kv_indptr, config = data
   384→
   385→    # Resolve Q
   386→    if Q_DTYPE == "fp8":
   387→        q_input, q_scale = quantize_fp8(q)
   388→    else:
   389→        q_input, q_scale = q, None
   390→
   391→    # Resolve KV
   392→    if KV_DTYPE == "fp8":
   393→        kv_buffer_fp8, kv_scale = kv_data["fp8"]
   394→        kv_input = kv_buffer_fp8
   395→    else:
   396→        kv_input, kv_scale = kv_data["bf16"], None
   397→
   398→    return _aiter_mla_decode(
   399→        q_input,
   400→        kv_input,
   401→        qo_indptr,
   402→        kv_indptr,
   403→        config,
   404→        q_scale=q_scale,
   405→        kv_scale=kv_scale,
   406→    )
   407→
   408→
   409→check_implementation = make_match_reference(ref_kernel, rtol=1e-01, atol=1e-01)
   410→

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**MLA Decode Architecture:**
1. **Three-regime routing**: The submission already implements matmul (small batch), ASM a8w8 (medium), and ASM a16w8 (large) paths — this is at the Python dispatch ceiling (~67-70µs). The leader at 33µs uses a single fused CK/ASM kernel with zero Python overhead.
2. **10% tolerance**: MLA has rtol=0.1, atol=0.1 — extremely loose. This means approximate computation is acceptable, opening doors for aggressive quantization (MXFP4 KV cache) or reduced-precision attention.
3. **The gap is dispatch overhead**: With 3 Python function calls (quantize + stage1 + reduce), each adding ~20-25µs of dispatch floor, the total cannot beat ~60µs from Python. A load_inline fused kernel could eliminate all 3 dispatch calls.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

   161→## Scalar Computations
   162→
   163→```c
   164→int stride_Q    = Q->stride(0) * Q->element_size() * max_seqlen_q;
   165→int stride_Page = KV->stride(0) * KV->element_size();
   166→uint32_t log2_page = (uint32_t)log2f(page_size);
   167→
   168→args.s_MQA       = gqa_ratio * max_seqlen_q;  // = 16 * 1 = 16
   169→args.s_kv_split  = kv_split;                   // = splitData.size(1)
   170→args.s_Q_Bs      = stride_Q;
   171→args.s_Bs        = stride_Page;
   172→args.s_log2_plen = log2_page;                  // = 0 for page_size=1
   173→args.out_16_nosplit = kv_split;                // same as s_kv_split
   174→```
   175→
   176→For a typical decode with `[total_q=bs, 16 heads, 576 qk_head_dim]` fp8:
   177→- `stride_Q = bs * 16 * 576 * 1 * 1 = bs * 9216` bytes (if contiguous)
   178→  - Actually: `Q.stride(0) * Q.element_size() * max_seqlen_q = (16*576) * 1 * 1 = 9216` bytes

   302→`mla_reduce_v1` is a CK-tile device kernel compiled into the aiter `.so`, NOT a pre-compiled `.co` file. It is launched via `<<<grid, threads, sharedmem, stream>>>` syntax from `csrc/kernels/mla/reduce.cu`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**MoE Optimization Landscape:**
1. **API ceiling confirmed**: 18 phases of experimentation exhausted all fused_moe parameters. The gap (154→110µs) requires architectural change.
2. **LDS Bridge concept**: In the 2-stage MoE (Gate+Up → SiLU → Down), the intermediate activations are written to HBM between stages. If we keep them in shared memory (LDS = Local Data Share on AMD), we eliminate one HBM round-trip per expert, which could save 20-40µs on MI355X.
3. **Pre-compiled kernels**: The runner has 182 pre-compiled CK kernels at `/home/runner/aiter/hsa/gfx950/fmoe_2stages/`. Directly loading and dispatching these via load_inline could bypass the Python fused_moe wrapper entirely.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The MoE load_inline approach is complex because it needs to handle expert routing, permutation, and two GEMM stages. Let me create a simpler first version that focuses on eliminating Python dispatch overhead by wrapping the aiter calls in C++:

     1→"""
     2→MXFP4 GEMM — load_inline with ROCWMMA MFMA for MI355X (gfx950).
     3→
     4→Uses AMD's rocWMMA library for native MFMA (Matrix Fused Multiply-Add) instructions.
     5→This should give significant speedup over naive load_inline.
     6→
     7→Based on official template-hip.py pattern from gpu-mode/reference-kernels.
     8→"""
     9→
    10→import os
    11→
    12→from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline
    13→
    14→
    15→os.environ["PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH"] = "gfx950"
    16→
    17→from task import input_t, output_t
    18→
    19→
    20→CPP_WRAPPER = """
    21→void mxfp4_gemm_rocwmma(
    22→    torch::Tensor A_packed,
    23→    torch::Tensor B_packed, 
    24→    torch::Tensor A_scale,
    25→    torch::Tensor B_scale,
    26→    torch::Tensor C
    27→);
    28→"""
    29→
    30→# ROCWMMA MFMA kernel for MI355X
    31→HIP_SRC = r"""
    32→#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
    33→#include <hip/amd_detail/amd_hip_fp8.h>
    34→#include <hip/amd_detail/amd_hip_bf16.h>
    35→#include <rocwmma/rocwmma.hpp>
    36→
    37→namespace rocwmma {
    38→
    39→// MI355X (gfx950) MFMA configuration
    40→// 16x16x2f16 = 16x16 matrix, 2 floats per instruction
    41→using I8x16x16x2 = matrix_layout::matrix_layout_enum;
    42→constexpr int BLOCK_M = 128;
    43→constexpr int BLOCK_N = 128;
    44→constexpr int BLOCK_K = 64;
    45→constexpr int WAVE_SIZE = 64;
    46→
    47→}
    48→
    49→// FP4 e2m1 to float
    50→__device__ inline float fp4_to_f32(uint8_t fp4) {
    51→    float vals[16] = {
    52→        0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 1.5f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 6.0f,
    53→        -0.0f, -0.5f, -1.0f, -1.5f, -2.0f, -3.0f, -4.0f, -6.0f
    54→    };
    55→    return vals[fp4 & 0xF];
    56→}
    57→
    58→__device__ inline float unpack_fp4(uint8_t packed, int idx) {
    59→    uint8_t nibble = (idx == 0) ? (packed & 0xF) : ((packed >> 4) & 0xF);
    60→    return fp4_to_f32(nibble);
    61→}
    62→
    63→__device__ inline float e8m0_to_f32(uint8_t e8m0) {
    64→    if (e8m0 == 0) return 0.0f;
    65→    if (e8m0 == 255) return 0.0f;
    66→    return exp2f((float)((int)e8m0 - 127));
    67→}
    68→
    69→// Simplified block-wise GEMM with lifted scales
    70→// Uses register blocking instead of shared memory for simplicity
    71→__global__ void mxfp4_gemm_kernel(
    72→    const uint8_t* A,
    73→    const uint8_t* B,
    74→    const uint8_t* As,
    75→    const uint8_t* Bs,
    76→    __hip_bfloat16* C,
    77→    int M, int N, int K
    78→) {
    79→    int bx = blockIdx.x;
    80→    int by = blockIdx.y;
    81→    int tx = threadIdx.x;
    82→    int ty = threadIdx.y;
    83→    
    84→    constexpr int BLOCK = 16;
    85→    
    86→    int row = bx * BLOCK + tx;
    87→    int col = by * BLOCK + ty;
    88→    
    89→    if (row >= M || col >= N) return;
    90→    
    91→    int k_blocks = K / 32;
    92→    int k_packed = K / 2;
    93→    
    94→    float result = 0.0f;
    95→    
    96→    for (int kb = 0; kb < k_blocks; kb++) {
    97→        float block_result = 0.0f;
    98→        
    99→        for (int kk = 0; kk < 32; kk++) {
   100→            int k_idx = kb * 32 + kk;
   101→            
   102→            int a_packed_idx = row * k_packed + k_idx / 2;
   103→            float a_val = unpack_fp4(A[a_packed_idx], k_idx % 2);
   104→            
   105→            int b_packed_idx = col * k_packed + k_idx / 2;
   106→            float b_val = unpack_fp4(B[b_packed_idx], k_idx % 2);
   107→            
   108→            block_result += a_val * b_val;
   109→        }
   110→        
   111→        // LIFTED scale
   112→        float a_scale = e8m0_to_f32(As[row * k_blocks + kb]);
   113→        float b_scale = e8m0_to_f32(Bs[col * k_blocks + kb]);
   114→        
   115→        result += block_result * a_scale * b_scale;
   116→    }
   117→    
   118→    C[row * N + col] = (__hip_bfloat16)result;
   119→}
   120→
   121→void mxfp4_gemm_rocwmma(
   122→    torch::Tensor A_packed,
   123→    torch::Tensor B_packed,
   124→    torch::Tensor A_scale,
   125→    torch::Tensor B_scale,
   126→    torch::Tensor C
   127→) {
   128→    int M = A_packed.size(0);
   129→    int K = A_packed.size(1) * 2;
   130→    int N = B_packed.size(0);
   131→    
   132→    dim3 blocks((M + 15) / 16, (N + 15) / 16);
   133→    dim3 threads(16, 16);
   134→    
   135→    mxfp4_gemm_kernel<<<blocks, threads>>>(
   136→        (const uint8_t*)A_packed.data_ptr(),
   137→        (const uint8_t*)B_packed.data_ptr(),
   138→        (const uint8_t*)A_scale.data_ptr(),
   139→        (const uint8_t*)B_scale.data_ptr(),
   140→        (__hip_bfloat16*)C.data_ptr(),
   141→        M, N, K
   142→    );
   143→}
   144→"""
   145→
   146→os.environ["CXX"] = "clang++"
   147→
   148→try:
   149→    module = load_inline(
   150→        name="mxfp4_gemm_rocwmma",
   151→        cpp_sources=[CPP_WRAPPER],
   152→        cuda_sources=[HIP_SRC],
   153→        functions=["mxfp4_gemm_rocwmma"],
   154→        verbose=False,
   155→        extra_cuda_cflags=["--offload-arch=gfx950", "-std=c++20", "-O3", "-I/opt/rocm/include"],
   156→        extra_ldflags=["-L/opt/rocm/lib", "-lrocwmma"],
   157→    )
   158→    HAS_ROCMWMA = True
   159→except:
   160→    # Fallback to simple load_inline without rocwmma
   161→    module = None
   162→    HAS_ROCMWMA = False
   163→
   164→
   165→def custom_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
   166→    """MXFP4 GEMM using load_inline HIP kernel."""
   167→    import torch
   168→    from aiter import dtypes
   169→    from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant
   170→    from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import e8m0_shuffle
   171→
   172→    A, B, B_q, B_shuffle, B_scale_sh = data
   173→
   174→    M, K = A.shape
   175→    N = B.shape[0]
   176→    k_scale_groups = K // 32
   177→
   178→    # Quantize A to MXFP4
   179→    A_fp4, A_scale = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(A.contiguous())
   180→
   181→    # Prepare scales
   182→    A_scale_bytes = A_scale[:M, :k_scale_groups].contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
   183→    A_scale_sh = e8m0_shuffle(A_scale_bytes.view(dtypes.fp8_e8m0))
   184→    A_scale_sh_bytes = A_scale_sh.view(torch.uint8)
   185→
   186→    # Get packed views
   187→    A_packed = A_fp4.view(torch.uint8)
   188→    B_packed = B_shuffle.view(torch.uint8)
   189→    B_scale_bytes = B_scale_sh.view(torch.uint8)
   190→
   191→    # Allocate output
   192→    C = torch.empty((M, N), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=A.device)
   193→
   194→    if module is not None:
   195→        # Use rocWMMA version
   196→        module.mxfp4_gemm_rocwmma(A_packed, B_packed, A_scale_sh_bytes, B_scale_bytes, C)
   197→    else:
   198→        # Fallback to aiter
   199→        import aiter
   200→
   201→        A_q_packed = A_fp4.view(dtypes.fp4x2)
   202→        C = aiter.gemm_a4w4(
   203→            A_q_packed,
   204→            B_shuffle,
   205→            A_scale_sh,
   206→            B_scale_sh,
   207→            dtype=dtypes.bf16,
   208→            bpreshuffle=True,
   209→        )
   210→
   211→    return C
   212→

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Cross-Conductor Discovery:**
1. The autoresearch conductor's "rocWMMA" kernel is actually still a naive 1-thread-per-element pattern (lines 86-119) — it doesn't use MFMA instructions despite the name. The `#include <rocwmma/rocwmma.hpp>` is imported but unused. The "lifted scale" optimization (line 115: `block_result * a_scale * b_scale`) is the key pattern though — accumulate the raw FP4 dot product first, then multiply by scales once per K block.
2. **Our v2 tiled kernel already does this correctly**: scales loaded once per tile to shared memory, applied after the inner K loop. What we're missing is the **MFMA instruction** (`V_MFMA_SCALE_F32_16X16X128_F8F6F4`) which does 16×16 matrix multiply in a single wavefront instruction.
3. **Key architectural insight**: The hardware MFMA for MXFP4 on gfx950 does FP4→F32 dequant + multiply + accumulate in ONE instruction — our software LUT decode + multiply is 3-4× slower per element. Using MFMA is the path to 4.3µs.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The `V_MFMA_SCALE_F32_16X16X128_F8F6F4` instruction is the breakthrough path but requires inline assembly in HIP. Let me create a GEMM v3 that attempts to use this via `__builtin_amdgcn_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4`:

    10→3. E8M0 scale: f32 = 2^(e8m0 - 127)
    11→4. dim3(16, 16) thread blocks

    27→    torch::Tensor B_packed,
    28→    torch::Tensor A_scale,
    29→    torch::Tensor B_scale,
    30→    torch::Tensor C

    34→HIP_SRC = r"""
    35→#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
    36→#include <hip/amd_detail/amd_hip_fp8.h>
    37→#include <hip/amd_detail/amd_hip_bf16.h>
    38→
    39→constexpr int BLOCK = 16;
    40→
    41→__device__ inline float fp4_to_f32(uint8_t v) {
    42→    float vals[16] = {
    43→        0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 1.5f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 6.0f,
    44→        -0.0f, -0.5f, -1.0f, -1.5f, -2.0f, -3.0f, -4.0f, -6.0f
    45→    };
    46→    return vals[v & 0xF];
    47→}
    48→
    49→__device__ inline float unpack_fp4(uint8_t packed, int idx) {
    50→    uint8_t nibble = (idx == 0) ? (packed & 0xF) : ((packed >> 4) & 0xF);
    51→    return fp4_to_f32(nibble);
    52→}
    53→
    54→__device__ inline float e8m0_to_f32(uint8_t e8m0) {
    55→    if (e8m0 == 0) return 0.0f;
    56→    if (e8m0 == 255) return 0.0f;
    57→    return exp2f((float)((int)e8m0 - 127));
    58→}
    59→
    60→__global__ void mxfp4_kernel(
    61→    const uint8_t* A,
    62→    const uint8_t* B,
    63→    const uint8_t* As,
    64→    const uint8_t* Bs,
    65→    __hip_bfloat16* C,
    66→    int M, int N, int K
    67→) {
    68→    int bx = blockIdx.x;
    69→    int by = blockIdx.y;
    70→    int tx = threadIdx.x;
    71→    int ty = threadIdx.y;
    72→
    73→    int row = bx * BLOCK + tx;
    74→    int col = by * BLOCK + ty;
    75→
    76→    if (row >= M || col >= N) return;
    77→
    78→    int k_blocks = K / 32;
    79→    int k_packed = K / 2;
    80→
    81→    float result = 0.0f;
    82→
    83→    for (int kb = 0; kb < k_blocks; kb++) {
    84→        float block_result = 0.0f;
    85→
    86→        for (int kk = 0; kk < 32; kk++) {
    87→            int k_idx = kb * 32 + kk;
    88→
    89→            int a_packed_idx = row * k_packed + k_idx / 2;
    90→            float a_val = unpack_fp4(A[a_packed_idx], k_idx % 2);
    91→
    92→            int b_packed_idx = col * k_packed + k_idx / 2;
    93→            float b_val = unpack_fp4(B[b_packed_idx], k_idx % 2);
    94→
    95→            block_result += a_val * b_val;
    96→        }
    97→
    98→        float a_scale = e8m0_to_f32(As[row * k_blocks + kb]);
    99→        float b_scale = e8m0_to_f32(Bs[col * k_blocks + kb]);
   100→
   101→        result += block_result * a_scale * b_scale;
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    C[row * N + col] = (__hip_bfloat16)result;
   105→}
   106→
   107→void mxfp4_gemm(
   108→    torch::Tensor A_packed,
   109→    torch::Tensor B_packed,
   110→    torch::Tensor A_scale,
   111→    torch::Tensor B_scale,
   112→    torch::Tensor C
   113→) {
   114→    int M = A_packed.size(0);
   115→    int K = A_packed.size(1) * 2;
   116→    int N = B_packed.size(0);
   117→
   118→    dim3 blocks((M + BLOCK - 1) / BLOCK, (N + BLOCK - 1) / BLOCK);
   119→    dim3 threads(BLOCK, BLOCK);
   120→
   121→    mxfp4_kernel<<<blocks, threads>>>(
   122→        (const uint8_t*)A_packed.data_ptr(),
   123→        (const uint8_t*)B_packed.data_ptr(),
   124→        (const uint8_t*)A_scale.data_ptr(),
   125→        (const uint8_t*)B_scale.data_ptr(),
   126→        (__hip_bfloat16*)C.data_ptr(),
   127→        M, N, K
   128→    );
   129→}
   130→"""
   131→
   132→os.environ["CXX"] = "clang++"
   133→
   134→module = load_inline(
   135→    name="mxfp4_gemm",
   136→    cpp_sources=[CPP_WRAPPER],
   137→    cuda_sources=[HIP_SRC],
   138→    functions=["mxfp4_gemm"],
   139→    verbose=False,
   140→    extra_cuda_cflags=["--offload-arch=gfx950", "-std=c++20", "-O3"],
   141→)
   142→
   143→
   144→def custom_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
   145→    """MXFP4 GEMM using pure load_inline HIP kernel."""
   146→    import torch
   147→    from aiter import dtypes
   148→    from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant
   149→    from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import e8m0_shuffle
   150→
   151→    A, B, B_q, B_shuffle, B_scale_sh = data
   152→
   153→    M, K = A.shape
   154→    N = B.shape[0]
   155→    k_scale_groups = K // 32
   156→
   157→    A_fp4, A_scale = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(A.contiguous())
   158→
   159→    k_scale_valid = k_scale_groups
   160→    A_scale_bytes = A_scale[:M, :k_scale_valid].contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
   161→    A_scale_sh = e8m0_shuffle(A_scale_bytes.view(dtypes.fp8_e8m0))
   162→    A_scale_sh_bytes = A_scale_sh.view(torch.uint8)
   163→
   164→    A_packed = A_fp4.view(torch.uint8)
   165→    B_packed = B_shuffle.view(torch.uint8)
   166→    B_scale_bytes = B_scale_sh.view(torch.uint8)
   167→
   168→    C = torch.empty((M, N), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=A.device)
   169→
   170→    module.mxfp4_gemm(A_packed, B_packed, A_scale_sh_bytes, B_scale_bytes, C)
   171→
   172→    return C
   173→
